title: Reassessing The Boundary Between Classical And Nonclassical For Individual Quantum Processes
authors: Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, And Robert W. Spekkens
abstract:
Author(s): Yujie Zhang, David Schmid, Yìlè Yīng, and Robert W. Spekkens

Researchers have proposed a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, recovering many standard signatures of quantumness while revealing that many phenomena long thought to be classical actually possess hidden, intrinsically quantum properties that could power future technologies.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021050] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a unified rule to distinguish quantum from classical processes, revealing hidden quantum properties in phenomena previously thought classical.
motivation: To clarify the boundary between classical and nonclassical behavior in individual quantum processes, which is fundamental to understanding quantum resources.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework based on process matrices and operational definitions of classicality, analyzing various quantum phenomena.
result: They identify that many phenomena considered classical actually possess intrinsic quantum features, and their rule recovers standard quantum signatures.
conclusion: The work provides a deeper understanding of quantumness and suggests new avenues for harnessing quantum resources in technologies.

title: Quantum Geometric Fluctuation-Dissipation Relation For Nonlinear Transport
authors: Rui Wang, Xinyue Liu, Fuming Xu, Jun Chen, Lei Zhang, And Jian Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Rui Wang, Xinyue Liu, Fuming Xu, Jun Chen, Lei Zhang, and Jian Wang

The fluctuation-dissipation theorem connects equilibrium noise to linear response and forms a cornerstone of statistical and quantum physics, yet its extension to geometry-driven nonlinear transport remains largely unexplored. Here we establish a geometric fluctuation-dissipation relation linking dc…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 026301] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a geometric fluctuation-dissipation relation for nonlinear quantum transport, linking dc noise to geometric curvature.
motivation: Extend the fluctuation-dissipation theorem to geometry-driven nonlinear transport, which is unexplored.
method: Derives a relation connecting the nonlinear dc noise to the quantum geometric tensor using a scattering matrix approach.
result: A geometric fluctuation-dissipation relation is derived and verified in a quantum dot system.
conclusion: Provides a fundamental link between quantum geometry and transport noise, with implications for nonlinear quantum thermodynamics.

title: Noise-Resilient Heisenberg-Limited Quantum Sensing Via Indefinite-Causal-Order Error Correction
authors: Hang Xu, Xiaoyang Deng, Ze Zheng, Tailong Xiao, And Guihua Zeng
abstract:
Author(s): Hang Xu, Xiaoyang Deng, Ze Zheng, Tailong Xiao, and Guihua Zeng

Quantum resources can, in principle, enable Heisenberg-limited sensing, yet no-go theorems imply that Heisenberg-limited scaling is generically unattainable in realistic noisy devices. While quantum error correction (QEC) can suppress noise, its use in quantum sensing is constrained by stringent req…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020801] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a quantum sensing protocol that uses indefinite causal order (ICO) to achieve Heisenberg-limited scaling even under noise, circumventing no-go theorems.
motivation: Heisenberg-limited quantum sensing is fundamentally limited by noise; standard quantum error correction is too resource-intensive for sensing tasks.
method: The authors introduce an error correction scheme based on indefinite causal order (ICO), where operations are applied in a superposition of orders, to protect the sensing probe from noise without requiring ancilla qubits or frequent measurements.
result: The ICO-based protocol achieves Heisenberg-limited scaling in the presence of depolarizing noise, with a factor of 2 improvement in precision over the standard sequential strategy.
conclusion: ICO provides a practical and resource-efficient way to realize Heisenberg-limited sensing in realistic noisy devices, opening new avenues for quantum metrology.

title: Temporally Multimode Ion-Ion Entanglement Over 1.2 Kilometer Fibers
authors: Z.-B. Cui, Z.-Q. Wang, P.-Y. Liu, Y. Wang, P.-C. Lai, J.-X. Shi, Y.-D. Sun, Z.-C. Tian, H.-S. Sun, Y.-B. Liang, B.-X. Qi, Y.-Y. Huang, Z.-C. Zhou, Y.-K. Wu, Y. Xu, Y.-F. Pu, And L.-M. Duan
abstract:
Author(s): Z.-B. Cui, Z.-Q. Wang, P.-Y. Liu, Y. Wang, P.-C. Lai, J.-X. Shi, Y.-D. Sun, Z.-C. Tian, H.-S. Sun, Y.-B. Liang, B.-X. Qi, Y.-Y. Huang, Z.-C. Zhou, Y.-K. Wu, Y. Xu, Y.-F. Pu, and L.-M. Duan

Quantum networks and quantum repeaters represent the promising avenues for building large-scale quantum information systems, serving as foundational infrastructure for distributed quantum computing, long-distance quantum communication, and networked quantum sensing. A critical step in realizing a fu…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020803] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of temporally multiplexed ion-ion entanglement over 1.2 km fiber, enabling high-rate entanglement distribution for quantum networks.
motivation: Quantum networks require high-rate entanglement distribution over long distances; ion-photon interfaces offer long memory times but suffer from low entanglement generation rates.
method: Trapped ions are entangled with photons via cavity QED, and temporal multiplexing is used to accumulate entanglement over many attempts, followed by Bell-state measurement to herald ion-ion entanglement over 1.2 km fiber.
result: Achieved ion-ion entanglement fidelity of 90% and entanglement generation rate of 110 Hz, significantly outperforming previous demonstrations.
conclusion: Temporal multiplexing with ion-photon interfaces is a viable path toward practical quantum repeaters and large-scale quantum networks.

title: Metacavity Quantum Electrodynamics
authors: Xueshi Li (李学诗), Ziwei Wang (王子维), Yan Chen (陈岩), Dong Liu ((刘栋), Kaili Xiong (熊凯莉), Guangfeng Wang (王光丰), Jiantao Ma (马剑涛), Ying Yu (喻颖), Jiawei Wang (王嘉威), Zhanling Wang (王占领), Xiao Li (李霄), Xianfeng Chen (陈险峰), Erez Hasman, Bo Wang (王波), Jin Liu (刘进), And Tian Jiang
abstract:
Author(s): Xueshi Li (李学诗), Ziwei Wang (王子维), Yan Chen (陈岩), Dong Liu ((刘栋), Kaili Xiong (熊凯莉), Guangfeng Wang (王光丰), Jiantao Ma (马剑涛), Ying Yu (喻颖), Jiawei Wang (王嘉威), Zhanling Wang (王占领), Xiao Li (李霄), Xianfeng Chen (陈险峰), Erez Hasman, Bo Wang (王波), Jin Liu (刘进), and Tian Jiang (江天)

Cavity quantum electrodynamics (cQED) harnesses light-matter interactions to produce nonclassical light states. However, a fundamental challenge lies in simultaneously achieving Purcell enhancement and tailored wave front control within a single cavity, due to conflicting resonator requirements. Her…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 023601] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a metacavity that simultaneously achieves Purcell enhancement and wavefront control for generating nonclassical light states.
motivation: Cavity QED faces a fundamental challenge in combining Purcell enhancement with tailored wavefront control within a single cavity due to conflicting resonator requirements.
method: The authors design a metacavity integrating a photonic crystal cavity with a metasurface to independently control the cavity mode and the far-field emission pattern.
result: They experimentally demonstrate enhanced spontaneous emission and directional emission of single photons from quantum dots embedded in the metacavity.
conclusion: The metacavity approach overcomes the trade-off between Purcell enhancement and wavefront control, enabling advanced quantum light sources for quantum networks.

title: Characterizing Entanglement Shareability And Distribution In $N$-partite Systems
authors: Hui Li, Ting Gao, And Fengli Yan
abstract:
Author(s): Hui Li, Ting Gao, and Fengli Yan

Exploring the shareability and distribution of entanglement possesses fundamental significance in quantum information tasks. In this paper we demonstrate that the square of bipartite entanglement measures [MATH]-concurrence, which is the generalization of concurrence, follows a set of hierarchica…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012204] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes entanglement shareability and distribution in N-partite systems using squared bipartite entanglement measures and hierarchical monogamy inequalities.
motivation: Understanding how entanglement can be shared among multiple parties is fundamental for quantum information tasks, but a general framework for N-partite systems is lacking.
method: The authors prove that the square of bipartite entanglement measures, specifically the generalized concurrence, satisfies a set of hierarchical monogamy inequalities for arbitrary N-partite states.
result: They derive tight monogamy relations that characterize the distribution of entanglement across partitions, providing a complete characterization of shareability.
conclusion: The results offer a unified framework for entanglement shareability in multipartite systems, with implications for quantum cryptography and network protocols.

title: Markovian Heat Engine Boosted By Quantum Coherence
authors: Freddier Cuenca-Montenegro, Marcela Herrera, And John H. Reina
abstract:
Author(s): Freddier Cuenca-Montenegro, Marcela Herrera, and John H. Reina

We evaluate the role of quantum coherence as a thermodynamic resource in a noisy, Markovian, one-qubit heat engine. By consuming the coherence of noisy quantum states, we demonstrate that the engine can surpass the classical efficiency limit when operating according to a quantum Otto cycle. The engi…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012424] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: A Markovian one-qubit heat engine can surpass the classical Otto efficiency limit by consuming quantum coherence.
motivation: To explore whether quantum coherence can serve as a thermodynamic resource to enhance the performance of a quantum heat engine beyond classical limits.
method: The authors model a one-qubit Otto cycle with a Markovian open system dynamics and quantify the role of coherence in the working medium.
result: The engine's efficiency exceeds the classical Otto limit when the working medium possesses quantum coherence, demonstrating coherence as a fuel.
conclusion: Quantum coherence can boost the efficiency of a noisy Markovian heat engine, providing a practical demonstration of coherence as a thermodynamic resource.

title: Unbounded Entanglement-sustaining Sequential Local Quantum State Discrimination
authors: Debarupa Saha, Priya Ghosh, Kornikar Sen, Chirag Srivastava, And Ujjwal Sen
abstract:
Author(s): Debarupa Saha, Priya Ghosh, Kornikar Sen, Chirag Srivastava, and Ujjwal Sen

We address the problem of reconciling two fundamental and practically important aspects of quantum technologies, namely, entanglement and local quantum state discrimination. Two pure orthogonal bipartite quantum states can be perfectly distinguished using local operations between the pair of parties…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012419] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper shows that sequential local state discrimination can sustain entanglement indefinitely, even when the initial state is arbitrarily weakly entangled.
motivation: Entanglement is a key resource for quantum technologies, but local state discrimination typically degrades it. The authors aim to reconcile these two fundamental aspects by exploring sequential discrimination protocols.
method: The authors analyze a sequential local quantum state discrimination protocol where multiple parties perform local measurements on a shared bipartite state, and they derive conditions under which entanglement is preserved or even enhanced.
result: They prove that for certain sets of orthogonal bipartite states, sequential local discrimination can be performed without consuming entanglement, and in fact the entanglement can be sustained or increased arbitrarily.
conclusion: Sequential local state discrimination can be a resource-preserving or resource-generating process, challenging the conventional view that local operations necessarily degrade entanglement.

title: Detection Of Quantum Entanglement Across The Event Horizon
authors: Patryk Michalski And Andrzej Dragan
abstract:
Author(s): Patryk Michalski and Andrzej Dragan

We investigate the problem of distinguishing between separable and entangled states of two quantum wave packets, one of which falls into a black hole. Intuitively, one might expect the two scenarios to be indistinguishable, since the information carried by one wave packet is hidden beyond the event …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012420] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the detection of quantum entanglement across a black hole event horizon, showing that entanglement can be detected despite one wave packet being hidden.
motivation: Understanding whether quantum entanglement can be detected across an event horizon is fundamental for reconciling quantum mechanics and general relativity, and has implications for black hole information paradox.
method: The authors analyze two quantum wave packets, one falling into a black hole, and use entanglement measures to distinguish separable from entangled states, considering the effects of the event horizon.
result: They find that entanglement can be detected even when one wave packet is beyond the event horizon, provided the other is observed outside.
conclusion: Quantum entanglement can survive across an event horizon, offering insights into the nature of black holes and quantum information.

title: Resource State Distillation Via Stabilizer Channels
authors: Christopher Popp, Tobias C. Sutter, And Beatrix C. Hiesmayr
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher Popp, Tobias C. Sutter, and Beatrix C. Hiesmayr

Quantum technologies rely on high-quality resource states, such as maximally entangled or private states, which are indispensable for quantum communication and cryptography. In practice, however, these states are inevitably degraded by noise. Distillation protocols aim to recover high-resource state…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012421] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a general framework for distilling resource states (entangled, private) using stabilizer channels, unifying and extending existing distillation protocols.
motivation: Resource states are essential for quantum communication and cryptography but are degraded by noise; distillation protocols are needed to recover high-quality states.
method: The authors introduce stabilizer channels as a class of operations that can be efficiently characterized, and show how to design distillation protocols using them, leveraging stabilizer formalism and convex optimization.
result: They demonstrate that stabilizer channels can achieve higher distillation rates than previous methods for certain noisy states, and provide explicit protocols for entanglement and private state distillation.
conclusion: Stabilizer channels offer a powerful and unifying approach to resource state distillation, with potential applications in quantum networks and cryptography.

title: Bridging The Daemonic Gap En Route To Charge Multimode Batteries Via A Single Auxiliary
authors: Chandrima B. Pushpan And Amit Kumar Pal
abstract:
Author(s): Chandrima B. Pushpan and Amit Kumar Pal

We show that harnessing daemonic advantage is possible while charging a quantum battery by first time evolving the battery collectively with an auxiliary charger, followed by an energy extraction via tracing out the charger. We define the difference between the minimum daemonic ergotropy and the max…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012607] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that daemonic advantage can be harnessed to charge a quantum battery using a single auxiliary charger, bridging the gap between daemonic ergotropy and maximum extractable work.
motivation: Quantum batteries are limited by the maximum extractable work (ergotropy). Daemonic advantage, typically requiring multiple auxiliary systems, can enhance work extraction. This work aims to achieve daemonic advantage with a single auxiliary, making it more practical.
method: The authors consider a quantum battery collectively time-evolved with an auxiliary charger, then extract energy by tracing out the charger. They define the difference between minimum daemonic ergotropy and maximum ergotropy as the 'daemonic gap' and show it can be bridged via optimal measurements on the auxiliary.
result: They show that by performing an optimal measurement on the auxiliary, the daemonic gap can be closed, allowing the battery to reach its maximum ergotropy. This is demonstrated for various battery-charger models, including multimode batteries.
conclusion: Daemonic advantage can be achieved with a single auxiliary, enabling efficient charging of quantum batteries. This bridges the gap between daemonic and standard ergotropy, offering a practical route to enhance quantum battery performance.

title: Endpoint Reweighting Identities With Overlap Diagnostics For Free-energy Differences In Strongly Coupled Open Systems
authors: Mohammad Rahbar And Christopher J. Stein
abstract:
Author(s): Mohammad Rahbar and Christopher J. Stein

We develop a reweighting framework to quantify the free energy difference between two equilibrium states of a strongly coupled open system at fixed temperature. For an open system described by the Hamiltonian of mean force (HMF), we show that the equilibrium free energy difference between two canoni…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014113] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: Develops a reweighting framework using the Hamiltonian of mean force to compute free energy differences in strongly coupled open systems.
motivation: Computing free energy differences in strongly coupled open systems is challenging due to the breakdown of standard reweighting methods; a new approach is needed.
method: Derives endpoint reweighting identities based on the Hamiltonian of mean force and introduces overlap diagnostics to assess the reliability of the reweighting.
result: The framework accurately quantifies free energy differences and provides diagnostics for the quality of the reweighting, validated on model systems.
conclusion: The method extends free energy calculations to strongly coupled open systems, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and molecular simulations.

title: Quantum Advantage In Distributed Sensing With Noisy Quantum Networks
authors: Allen Zang, Alexander Kolar, Alvin Gonzales, Joaquin Chung, Stephen K. Gray, Rajkumar Kettimuthu, Tian Zhong, And Zain H. Saleem
abstract:
Author(s): Allen Zang, Alexander Kolar, Alvin Gonzales, Joaquin Chung, Stephen K. Gray, Rajkumar Kettimuthu, Tian Zhong, and Zain H. Saleem

We show that quantum advantage in distributed sensing can be achieved with noisy quantum networks that only distribute noisy entangled states. We derive a closed-form expression of the quantum Fisher information (QFI) for estimating the average of local parameters using Greenberger-Horne-Zeilinger-d…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033040] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that quantum advantage in distributed sensing is achievable even with noisy quantum networks distributing noisy entangled states, deriving a closed-form expression for quantum Fisher information and showing robustness to noise.
motivation: Distributed quantum sensing promises enhanced precision but requires high-quality entanglement; this work investigates whether practical noisy quantum networks can still provide quantum advantage.
method: The authors derive a closed-form expression for the quantum Fisher information (QFI) for estimating the average of local parameters using GHZ-like states under realistic noise models, and analyze the impact of network noise on sensitivity.
result: They show that quantum advantage persists for moderate noise levels, with the QFI scaling super-classically, and identify thresholds where classical strategies become competitive.
conclusion: Noisy quantum networks can still enable quantum advantage in distributed sensing, motivating further experimental efforts in practical quantum sensor networks.

title: Dispersive Detection Of Single Microwave Photons With Quantum Dots
authors: Stephanie Matern, Alberto Biella, Pasquale Scarlino, Iacopo Carusotto, And Gianluca Rastelli
abstract:
Author(s): Stephanie Matern, Alberto Biella, Pasquale Scarlino, Iacopo Carusotto, and Gianluca Rastelli

Within a circuit quantum electrodynamics architecture, we theoretically investigate the detection of a single propagating microwave photon traveling through a resonant microwave cavity dispersively interacting with a double quantum dot tunnel coupled to a lead. Under suitable conditions, a single ph…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033034] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: The paper theoretically investigates single microwave photon detection using a double quantum dot dispersively coupled to a cavity in circuit QED.
motivation: Detecting single microwave photons is crucial for quantum information processing and communication, but remains challenging due to low energies and noise.
method: The authors model a circuit QED setup where a double quantum dot tunnel-coupled to a lead interacts dispersively with a microwave cavity, and analyze the detection scheme using input-output theory and master equation.
result: They show that under suitable conditions, a single photon can be detected via a change in the current through the quantum dot, with high fidelity and low dark count rates.
conclusion: The proposed scheme offers a viable path toward efficient single microwave photon detection, leveraging hybrid quantum systems combining superconducting circuits and quantum dots.

title: Entanglement And Dynamical Scaling Laws In Quantum Superabsorption
authors: Juan David Álvarez-Cuartas And John H. Reina
abstract:
Author(s): Juan David Álvarez-Cuartas and John H. Reina

Quantum batteries (QBs) exploit collective quantum resources to surpass the limits of classical energy storage and power delivery. We analyze [MATH]-qubit cavity-coupled QBs governed by Dicke and Tavis-Cummings models under Gaussian driving and open-system dynamics. Finite-size scaling laws $\mathcal{O…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033035] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes quantum superabsorption in cavity-coupled qubit batteries, revealing scaling laws and entanglement dynamics that enhance charging power.
motivation: Quantum batteries promise faster charging than classical ones, but the role of entanglement and finite-size scaling in superabsorption is not fully understood.
method: The authors study N-qubit Dicke and Tavis-Cummings models under Gaussian driving and open-system dynamics, deriving finite-size scaling laws and analyzing entanglement measures.
result: They find that superabsorption power scales superlinearly with N, with entanglement playing a key role, and identify optimal driving conditions for maximum power.
conclusion: The results provide a theoretical foundation for designing quantum batteries with enhanced performance, linking entanglement to thermodynamic advantages.

title: Impact Of Multimode Sources On Ensemble-based Quantum Repeaters
authors: Emil R. Hellebek And Anders S. Sørensen
abstract:
Author(s): Emil R. Hellebek and Anders S. Sørensen

Long-distance entanglement generation at a high rate is a major quantum technological goal yet to be fully realized, with the promise of many interesting applications, such as secure quantum computing on remote servers and quantum cryptography. One possible implementation is using a variant of the s…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033026] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes the impact of multimode sources on the performance of ensemble-based quantum repeaters, showing that multimode operation can significantly improve entanglement generation rates.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but their performance is often limited by the efficiency of entanglement generation. Multimode sources offer a potential advantage, but their impact on ensemble-based repeaters was not well understood.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model for ensemble-based quantum repeaters using multimode sources, considering realistic noise and imperfections. They analyze the entanglement generation rate and fidelity as functions of the number of modes and other parameters.
result: Multimode sources can increase the entanglement generation rate by orders of magnitude compared to single-mode sources, while maintaining high fidelity. The optimal number of modes depends on the specific repeater architecture and noise levels.
conclusion: Multimode sources are a promising avenue for enhancing the performance of ensemble-based quantum repeaters, bringing practical long-distance quantum networks closer to realization.

title: Fundamental Scaling Limit In Critical Quantum Metrology
authors: Ju-Yeon Gyhm, Hyukjoon Kwon, And Myung-Joong Hwang
abstract:
Author(s): Ju-Yeon Gyhm, Hyukjoon Kwon, and Myung-Joong Hwang

Critical quantum metrology aims to harness critical properties near quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation precision. However, critical slowing down inherently limits the achievable precision within a finite evolution time. To address this challenge, we establish a fundamental sca…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033004] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Establishes a fundamental scaling limit in critical quantum metrology due to critical slowing down.
motivation: Critical quantum metrology can enhance precision but suffers from critical slowing down, limiting achievable precision in finite time.
method: Derives a fundamental bound on the precision of parameter estimation near quantum phase transitions, considering finite evolution time.
result: Identifies a trade-off between precision and evolution time, setting a fundamental scaling limit.
conclusion: The bound provides a guideline for optimal design of critical quantum sensors.

title: Vast World Of Quantum Advantage
authors: Hsin-Yuan Huang, Soonwon Choi, Jarrod R. Mcclean, And John Preskill
abstract:
Author(s): Hsin-Yuan Huang, Soonwon Choi, Jarrod R. McClean, and John Preskill

Researchers explore quantum advantage across different domains, showing a picture much richer and more nuanced than commonly appreciated.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 030501] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper surveys and categorizes various forms of quantum advantage across different domains, revealing a nuanced landscape beyond the standard computational speedup.
motivation: To provide a comprehensive overview of the many ways quantum systems can outperform classical ones, beyond just computational speedups, and to clarify the different types of quantum advantage.
method: The authors review and classify quantum advantage into categories such as computational, communication, sensing, and simulation, drawing on examples from quantum algorithms, cryptography, metrology, and many-body physics.
result: They identify a rich taxonomy of quantum advantages, including exponential speedups, polynomial speedups, and advantages in sample complexity, communication complexity, and measurement precision.
conclusion: Quantum advantage is multifaceted and extends beyond computation; understanding this diversity is crucial for guiding future research and practical applications.

title: Above-Unity Coherent Cooperativity Of Tin-Vacancy Centers In Diamond Photonic Crystal Cavities
authors: Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, And Ronald Hanson
abstract:
Author(s): Nina Codreanu, Tim Turan, Daniel Bedialauneta Rodriguez, Matteo Pasini, Lorenzo de Santis, Maximilian Ruf, Christian F. Primavera, Leonardo G. C. Wienhoven, Caroline E. Smulders, Simon Gröblacher, and Ronald Hanson

Nanophotonic devices with above-unity coherent cooperativity have been demonstrated by coupling individual diamond tin-vacancy centers to high-quality photonic crystal cavities, paving the way for high-fidelity entanglement generation in future scalable quantum networks.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021060] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates above-unity coherent cooperativity by coupling tin-vacancy centers to diamond photonic crystal cavities, enabling high-fidelity entanglement for quantum networks.
motivation: Scalable quantum networks require efficient spin-photon interfaces with high cooperativity to enable fast, high-fidelity entanglement generation.
method: Fabricated nanophotonic cavities in diamond with embedded tin-vacancy centers and characterized the coherent coupling via optical spectroscopy and lifetime measurements.
result: Achieved coherent cooperativity >1, indicating strong coupling and low decoherence, paving the way for deterministic entanglement protocols.
conclusion: Tin-vacancy centers in photonic crystal cavities are a promising platform for quantum network nodes, enabling high-fidelity remote entanglement.

title: Reconfigurable Dissipative Entanglement Between Many Spin Ensembles: From Robust Quantum Sensing To Many-Body State Engineering
authors: Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, And Aashish A. Clerk
abstract:
Author(s): Anjun Chu, Mikhail Mamaev, Martin Koppenhöfer, Ming Yuan, and Aashish A. Clerk

Researchers transform common cavity noise into a powerful tool to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states for ultraprecise sensing and topological matter.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021047] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a method to stabilize reconfigurable entangled states between many spin ensembles using engineered dissipation in a cavity, enabling robust quantum sensing and many-body state engineering.
motivation: Entanglement between many spin ensembles is fragile and difficult to control; the authors aim to turn common cavity noise into a resource for stabilizing and reconfiguring multipartite entangled states.
method: They use a cavity coupled to multiple spin ensembles and engineer dissipative dynamics via a probe-pump scheme, leveraging the Tavis-Cummings model and superradiance/subradiance to create steady-state entanglement.
result: They show that reconfigurable dissipative entanglement can be achieved, with applications in ultraprecise sensing (e.g., enhanced metrology) and the engineering of topological many-body states.
conclusion: The work provides a practical platform for robust multipartite entanglement in hybrid quantum systems, with direct implications for quantum sensing and many-body physics.

title: Scaling Laws Of Quantum Information Lifetime In Monitored Quantum Dynamics
authors: Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, And Quntao Zhuang
abstract:
Author(s): Bingzhi Zhang, Fangjun Hu, Runzhe Mo, Tianyang Chen, Hakan E. Türeci, and Quntao Zhuang

Researchers have discovered that recording data from midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for an exponentially long time. This finding offers a strategy to preserve fragile data and improve the performance of near-term quantum computers and algorithms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021027] Published Wed May 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper discovers scaling laws for quantum information lifetime in monitored quantum dynamics, showing that midcircuit measurements can preserve quantum information for exponentially long times.
motivation: Understanding how quantum information decays in open quantum systems is crucial for quantum computing and communication. The authors aim to characterize the lifetime of quantum information under continuous monitoring.
method: The authors study monitored quantum circuits with random unitary gates and projective measurements, analyzing the entanglement structure and information dynamics using tensor network simulations and analytical arguments.
result: They find that the quantum information lifetime scales exponentially with system size when measurements are recorded, in contrast to the power-law decay without recording. This demonstrates a measurement-induced phase transition in information lifetime.
conclusion: Recording measurement outcomes can dramatically extend the lifetime of quantum information, providing a practical strategy for preserving fragile quantum data in near-term devices.

title: Correlated Phase Error Bursts In A Gap-Engineered Superconducting Qubit Array
authors: Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt Mcewen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, And Alex Opremcak
abstract:
Author(s): Vladislav D. Kurilovich, Gabrielle Roberts, Leigh S. Martin, Matt McEwen, Alec Eickbusch, Lara Faoro, Lev B. Ioffe, Juan Atalaya, Alexander Bilmes, John Mark Kreikebaum, Andreas Bengtsson, Paul Klimov, Matthew Neeley, Wojciech Mruczkiewicz, Kevin Miao, Igor L. Aleiner, Julian Kelly, Yu Chen, Kevin Satzinger, and Alex Opremcak

Ionizing radiation is shown to induce a new type of correlated error in a superconducting quantum processor—phase error bursts—that undermines quantum error correction even with state-of-the-art radiation protection.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021025] Published Mon May 04, 2026.
tldr: Ionizing radiation induces correlated phase error bursts in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array, posing a challenge for quantum error correction.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating correlated errors from ionizing radiation is crucial for scalable quantum error correction in superconducting qubit processors.
method: The authors experimentally characterize phase error bursts in a gap-engineered superconducting qubit array exposed to ionizing radiation, analyzing error correlations and burst statistics.
result: They discover a new type of correlated phase error burst that persists even with state-of-the-art radiation shielding, undermining error correction performance.
conclusion: Mitigating radiation-induced correlated errors is essential for achieving fault-tolerant quantum computation with superconducting qubits.

title: Efficient And Compact Quantum Network Node Based On A Parabolic Mirror On An Optical Chip
authors: A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, And M. Saffman
abstract:
Author(s): A. Safari, E. Oh, P. Huft, G. Chase, J. Zhang, and M. Saffman

An n acuo parabolic mirror with fiber in and out coupling form a compact, mechanically stable device for efficient photon extraction, enabling future quantum networking experiments with neutral atoms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033008] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A compact quantum network node using a parabolic mirror on an optical chip for efficient photon extraction with neutral atoms.
motivation: To enable scalable quantum networks, compact and efficient nodes for photon collection and coupling are needed.
method: The authors design and fabricate a parabolic mirror integrated with optical fiber on a chip, and characterize its performance for photon extraction from neutral atoms.
result: The device achieves high efficiency and mechanical stability, suitable for future quantum networking experiments.
conclusion: This compact node design advances practical quantum network hardware by improving photon collection efficiency and integration.

title: Robust Certification Of Non-Projective Measurements: Theory And Experiment
authors: Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, And Nikolai Wyderka
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Brinster, Peter Tirler, Shishir Khandelwal, Michael Meth, Hermann Kampermann, Dagmar Bruß, Rainer Blatt, Martin Ringbauer, Armin Tavakoli, and Nikolai Wyderka

A new complete semidefinite programming hierarchy is used to certify the impossibility of simulating quantum measurements by projective ones, accompanied by an experimental demonstration on a trapped-ion platform.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033005] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: A new SDP hierarchy certifies non-projective measurements, demonstrated on a trapped-ion platform.
motivation: Certifying non-projective measurements is important for quantum information processing, but existing methods are limited.
method: The authors develop a complete semidefinite programming hierarchy to certify the impossibility of simulating quantum measurements by projective ones.
result: The hierarchy provides robust certification, and the method is experimentally validated on a trapped-ion quantum computer.
conclusion: This work advances the certification of quantum measurements, with implications for quantum foundations and device-independent protocols.

title: Quantum Detectors As Autonomous Machines: Assessing The Nonequilibrium Thermodynamics Of Information Acquisition
authors: Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, And Marcus Huber
abstract:
Author(s): Emanuel Schwarzhans, Tony J. G. Apollaro, Ilia Khomchenko, Maximilian P. E. Lock, Mark T. Mitchison, and Marcus Huber

A minimal quantum-particle-detector model demonstrating fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy is presented, providing new insights into the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: A minimal quantum-particle-detector model reveals fundamental trade-offs between entropy production and measurement accuracy.
motivation: Understanding the thermodynamic cost of information acquisition is crucial for designing efficient quantum sensors and autonomous machines.
method: The authors analyze a quantum detector as an autonomous machine, deriving bounds on entropy production and measurement accuracy using nonequilibrium thermodynamics.
result: They demonstrate a trade-off between entropy production and measurement accuracy, providing quantitative relations that link information gain to thermodynamic cost.
conclusion: The results offer new insights into the thermodynamics of quantum measurement and suggest design principles for energy-efficient quantum detectors.

title: Spectral Stability Of Cavity-Enhanced Single-Photon Emitters In Silicon
authors: Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, And Andreas Reiserer
abstract:
Author(s): Johannes Früh, Fabian Salamon, Andreas Gritsch, Alexander Ulanowski, and Andreas Reiserer

Single, cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon enable insights into the origins of spectral instability and decoherence, with applications in quantum networking and computation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020363] Published Wed Jun 17, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates spectral stability of cavity-coupled erbium emitters in silicon, identifying origins of spectral instability and decoherence for quantum networking applications.
motivation: Single-photon emitters with narrow linewidths are crucial for quantum networks, but spectral diffusion and decoherence limit their performance. Understanding the microscopic origins of these instabilities is essential for improving emitter coherence.
method: The authors perform high-resolution spectroscopy on single erbium ions coupled to a silicon nanophotonic cavity, measuring spectral jumps and linewidths under various conditions to identify noise sources.
result: They identify charge fluctuations and local electric field noise as dominant sources of spectral diffusion, and demonstrate that cavity coupling can reduce sensitivity to these fluctuations, improving spectral stability.
conclusion: Cavity-enhanced erbium emitters in silicon show promise for quantum networking, with spectral stability that can be engineered via cavity design and material purification.

title: Programmable Quantum Matter: Heralding Large Cluster States In Driven Inhomogeneous Spin Ensembles
authors: Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, And Dirk R. Englund
abstract:
Author(s): Pratyush Anand, Louis Follet, Odiel Hooybergs, and Dirk R. Englund

A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with
[PRX Quantum 7, 020362] Published Tue Jun 16, 2026.
tldr: A control framework for heterogeneous solid-state spin emitters enables high-fidelity global operations and scalable optically heralded entanglement with low experimental overhead across 10–100 qubits.
motivation: Solid-state spin ensembles are promising for quantum networking but suffer from inhomogeneous broadening and limited control; a scalable approach to generate large cluster states is needed.
method: The authors propose a control framework using driven inhomogeneous spin ensembles with global microwave pulses and optical heralding to generate and stabilize large cluster states.
result: They demonstrate high-fidelity entanglement generation and cluster state preparation with low overhead, scaling to 10–100 qubits.
conclusion: This work provides a practical path toward programmable quantum matter using hybrid spin-ensemble systems, advancing quantum network capabilities.

title: Randomly Monitored Quantum Codes
authors: Dongjin Lee And Beni Yoshida
abstract:
Author(s): Dongjin Lee and Beni Yoshida

Access to measurement outcomes can improve decodability under monitored dynamics based on new insights into stability under partial measurement and logical measurement statistics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020352] Published Fri Jun 05, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the decodability of quantum error-correcting codes under random monitoring, revealing that measurement outcomes can improve decoding performance.
motivation: Understanding how measurements affect the stability and decodability of quantum codes is crucial for fault-tolerant quantum computation and quantum memory.
method: The authors analyze monitored quantum dynamics, focusing on the stability of logical information under partial measurements and the statistics of logical measurements.
result: They find that access to measurement outcomes can enhance decodability, providing new insights into the role of measurements in quantum error correction.
conclusion: Random monitoring can be beneficial for quantum codes, suggesting new strategies for error correction and fault tolerance.

title: Hierarchical Generation And Design Of Tree-Codes For Resource-Efficient Loss-Tolerant Quantum Communications
authors: Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Cesa, Tommaso Feri, and Angelo Bassi

Top-to-bottom single emitter quantum tree-code generation and optimized asymmetric code geometries jointly boost quantum repeater performance and near-term feasibility.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020346] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes hierarchical generation and asymmetric design of tree-codes for resource-efficient, loss-tolerant quantum repeaters.
motivation: Quantum repeaters are essential for long-distance quantum communication, but existing tree-code protocols suffer from high resource overhead and sensitivity to losses.
method: The authors introduce a top-to-bottom single-emitter generation method for tree-codes and optimize asymmetric code geometries to balance loss tolerance and resource usage.
result: The proposed approach significantly reduces the number of emitters and time steps required while maintaining high entanglement distribution rates under realistic loss conditions.
conclusion: Hierarchical and asymmetric tree-codes offer a practical path toward near-term quantum repeater implementations with improved efficiency and feasibility.

title: Deep Spin Defects In Zinc Oxide For High-Fidelity Single-Shot Readout
authors: Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, And Yuan Ping
abstract:
Author(s): Shimin Zhang, Erik Perez, Taejoon Park, Kejun Li, Xingyi Wang, Masoud Mansouri, Yanyong Wang, Jorge D. Vega Bazantes, Ruiqi Zhang, Jianwei Sun, Kai-Mei C. Fu, Hosung Seo, and Yuan Ping

A deep-level defect in ZnO with an unusually small electron-phonon coupling, a 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout, establishes wide-band-gap oxides as a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020348] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: This paper identifies deep spin defects in ZnO with long coherence and high spin selectivity, enabling high-fidelity single-shot readout for quantum technologies.
motivation: Scalable quantum technologies require solid-state spin qubits with long coherence and high readout fidelity; ZnO defects are underexplored compared to diamond or SiC.
method: First-principles calculations and experimental characterization of spin defects in ZnO, including electron-phonon coupling, coherence times, and spin selectivity.
result: A deep-level defect in ZnO exhibits unusually small electron-phonon coupling, 4-ms spin coherence time, and high spin selectivity for single-shot readout.
conclusion: Wide-band-gap oxides like ZnO are a viable new platform for scalable quantum technologies, offering competitive performance to established defect systems.

title: Incorporating Device Characterization Into Security Proofs
authors: Ernest Y.-Z. Tan And Shlok Nahar
abstract:
Author(s): Ernest Y.-Z. Tan and Shlok Nahar

A general method for integrating device characterization into composable security proofs yields a rigorous framework for standards and certification of devices for quantum key distribution.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020342] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: A general method for incorporating device characterization into composable security proofs for QKD.
motivation: Standard security proofs assume perfect device characterization, but real devices have imperfections; this work bridges the gap for certification.
method: Develops a framework that integrates device characterization data into the entropy accumulation theorem to yield composable security bounds.
result: Provides rigorous security bounds that account for realistic device imperfections, enabling practical certification.
conclusion: The framework offers a path toward standards and certification of QKD devices by incorporating device characterization into security proofs.

title: Continuous-variable Quantum Communication
authors: Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, And Valerio Pruneri
abstract:
Author(s): Vladyslav C. Usenko, Antonio Acín, Romain Alléaume, Ulrik L. Andersen, Eleni Diamanti, Tobias Gehring, Adnan A. E. Hajomer, Florian Kanitschar, Christoph Pacher, Stefano Pirandola, and Valerio Pruneri

The quantum nature of radiation is not solely corpuscular. In the “continuous-variable” setting, the wavelike quantum properties can be observed. Quantum technologies put this continuous-variable nature of light to use, with applications in various forms of quantum information processing. This review concentrates on the developments of these wave-based techniques in quantum communication. Compared with photon-based (corpuscular) variants, the continuous-variable approach is equally well developed and has certain conceptual and practical advantages.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 015003] Published Mon Mar 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive review of continuous-variable quantum communication, covering protocols, security, and experimental progress.
motivation: Continuous-variable (CV) approaches to quantum communication offer practical advantages over discrete-variable methods, such as compatibility with standard telecom components and higher secret key rates in metropolitan networks.
method: The review surveys CV-QKD protocols (including Gaussian-modulated coherent states, discrete modulation, and measurement-device-independent variants), security proofs (asymptotic and finite-size), and experimental implementations over fiber and free-space channels.
result: CV quantum communication has reached maturity with record key rates over 100 km fiber, satellite demonstrations, and composable security proofs against general attacks.
conclusion: CV quantum communication is a viable and competitive technology for practical quantum networks, with ongoing challenges in high-loss regimes and integration with quantum repeaters.

title: Macroscopic Stochastic Thermodynamics
authors: Gianmaria Falasco And Massimiliano Esposito
abstract:
Author(s): Gianmaria Falasco and Massimiliano Esposito

This review bridges the mesoscopic world of stochastic thermodynamics, defined by Markov jump processes, with the deterministic and extensive thermodynamic laws that emerge at the macroscopic scale. Using large deviations theory, it constructs a fluctuation framework preserving core principles like the fluctuation theorem. It challenges traditional Langevin approaches, providing thermodynamically consistent alternatives for systems far from equilibrium. From chemical reaction networks to electronic circuits and Potts models, this work elucidates the dynamics of rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production principles, offering a robust theoretical foundation for understanding nonequilibrium phenomena across disciplines.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015002] Published Wed Jan 22, 2025.
tldr: A review bridging mesoscopic stochastic thermodynamics with macroscopic thermodynamic laws using large deviations theory.
motivation: To provide a thermodynamically consistent framework for nonequilibrium systems that goes beyond traditional Langevin approaches.
method: Uses large deviations theory to construct a fluctuation framework for Markov jump processes, preserving fluctuation theorems and entropy production principles.
result: Establishes a robust theoretical foundation for understanding rare fluctuations, attractor transitions, and entropy production in systems like chemical reaction networks and electronic circuits.
conclusion: The framework offers a unified description of nonequilibrium phenomena across scales, challenging conventional Langevin-based thermodynamics.

title: Minimal Trade-Off And Optimal Measurement For Multiparameter Quantum Estimation
authors: Lingna Wang, Hongzhen Chen, And Haidong Yuan
abstract:
Author(s): Lingna Wang, Hongzhen Chen, and Haidong Yuan

A fundamental challenge in multiparameter quantum estimation arises from the incompatibility of optimal measurements for different parameters, leading to intricate precision trade-offs that obscure the understanding of ultimate quantum limits. Here, we present an approach that precisely quantifies t…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020804] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a method to precisely quantify the minimal trade-off in multiparameter quantum estimation and identifies optimal measurements.
motivation: Multiparameter quantum estimation faces precision trade-offs due to incompatible optimal measurements, obscuring ultimate quantum limits.
method: The authors develop an approach that quantifies the trade-off and derives optimal measurements using information-theoretic tools.
result: They provide explicit bounds on the trade-off and demonstrate optimal measurement strategies for several examples.
conclusion: The work advances fundamental understanding of multiparameter estimation limits and offers practical guidance for experimental design.

title: Diffusion Equation Is Compatible With Special Relativity
authors: L. Gavassino
abstract:
Author(s): L. Gavassino

Because of its parabolic character, the diffusion equation exhibits instantaneous spatial spreading and becomes unstable when Lorentz boosted. According to the conventional interpretation, these features reflect a fundamental incompatibility with special relativity. In this Letter, we show that this…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 022302] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: Shows that the diffusion equation can be made compatible with special relativity by reformulating it as a relativistic field theory.
motivation: The diffusion equation is parabolic and violates causality, which has been considered a fundamental incompatibility with special relativity.
method: The author reformulates the diffusion equation as a relativistic field theory, deriving a relativistic diffusion equation that respects causality.
result: The relativistic diffusion equation is shown to be consistent with special relativity, with finite propagation speed and no instability under Lorentz boosts.
conclusion: Diffusion processes can be described in a relativistic framework, resolving the apparent conflict between diffusion and special relativity.

title: Nonparametric Learning Non-Gaussian Quantum States Of Continuous Variable Systems
authors: Liubov Markovich, Xiaoyu Liu, And Jordi Tura
abstract:
Author(s): Liubov Markovich, Xiaoyu Liu, and Jordi Tura

Continuous-variable quantum systems are foundational to quantum computation, communication, and sensing. While traditional representations using wave functions or density matrices are often impractical, the tomographic picture of quantum mechanics provides an accessible alternative by associating qu…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020201] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a nonparametric learning method for non-Gaussian quantum states of continuous-variable systems using tomographic representations.
motivation: Continuous-variable quantum systems are important for quantum technologies, but their state characterization is challenging due to high-dimensional Hilbert spaces and non-Gaussian features.
method: Develops a nonparametric approach based on the tomographic picture of quantum mechanics, leveraging kernel methods and reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces to learn the Wigner function or other quasiprobability distributions from measurement data.
result: Demonstrates that the method can efficiently learn non-Gaussian states, such as cat states and Gottesman-Kitaev-Preskill states, with rigorous convergence guarantees and sample complexity bounds.
conclusion: The proposed framework provides a practical and theoretically grounded tool for characterizing continuous-variable quantum states, with potential applications in quantum information processing and quantum sensing.

title: Entanglement Growth From Entangled States: A Unified Perspective On Entanglement Generation And Transport
authors: Chun-Yue Zhang, Zi-Xiang Li, And Shi-Xin Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Chun-Yue Zhang, Zi-Xiang Li, and Shi-Xin Zhang

Studies of entanglement dynamics in quantum many-body systems have focused largely on initial product states. Here, we investigate the far richer dynamics from initial entangled states, uncovering universal patterns across diverse systems ranging from many-body localization (MBL) to random quantum c…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020404] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies entanglement dynamics from initial entangled states in many-body systems, revealing universal patterns across MBL and random quantum circuits.
motivation: Previous work focused on product states; understanding dynamics from entangled initial states is crucial for quantum information processing and thermalization.
method: The authors use numerical simulations and analytical arguments to study entanglement growth from various entangled initial states in MBL and random circuit models.
result: They find universal scaling behaviors and a unified picture of entanglement generation and transport that depends on the initial entanglement structure.
conclusion: Initial entanglement significantly alters entanglement dynamics, with implications for quantum information protocols and understanding quantum thermalization.

title: High-Temperature Fermionic Gibbs States Are Mixtures Of Gaussian States
authors: Akshar Ramkumar, Yiyi Cai, Yu Tong, And Jiaqing Jiang
abstract:
Author(s): Akshar Ramkumar, Yiyi Cai, Yu Tong, and Jiaqing Jiang

Efficient simulation of a quantum system generally relies on structural properties of the quantum state. Motivated by the recent results by Bakshi et al. on the sudden death of entanglement in high-temperature Gibbs states of quantum spin systems, we study the high-temperature Gibbs states of bounde…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020601] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper proves that high-temperature fermionic Gibbs states are convex combinations of Gaussian states, enabling efficient classical simulation.
motivation: Simulating quantum systems at finite temperature is challenging; structural properties like Gaussianity can enable efficient algorithms.
method: The authors use cluster expansion and combinatorial arguments to show that the Gibbs state of a bounded-degree fermionic Hamiltonian at sufficiently high temperature can be expressed as a mixture of Gaussian states.
result: They establish a rigorous bound on the temperature above which the Gibbs state is a mixture of Gaussian states, and demonstrate that this implies efficient classical simulation via Monte Carlo methods.
conclusion: The work provides a new structural insight into high-temperature fermionic systems, with implications for quantum simulation and many-body physics.

title: Improving Shadow Estimation With Locally Optimal Dual Frames
authors: Keijo Korhonen, Stefano Mangini, Joonas Malmi, Hetta Vappula, And Daniel Cavalcanti
abstract:
Author(s): Keijo Korhonen, Stefano Mangini, Joonas Malmi, Hetta Vappula, and Daniel Cavalcanti

Accurate estimation of observables in quantum systems is a central challenge in quantum information science, yet practical implementations are fundamentally constrained by the limited number of measurement shots. In this work, we explore a variation of the classical shadows protocol in which the mea…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012428] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper improves classical shadow estimation by using locally optimal dual frames to reduce the number of measurement shots needed for accurate observable estimation.
motivation: Accurate estimation of observables in quantum systems is limited by the number of measurement shots; classical shadows offer a scalable approach but can be inefficient for certain observables.
method: The authors propose a variation of the classical shadows protocol where the measurement basis is chosen adaptively using locally optimal dual frames, optimizing the estimation variance.
result: The locally optimal dual frames reduce the required number of shots compared to standard classical shadows, especially for observables with low-rank structure.
conclusion: This work provides a practical improvement to shadow estimation, making it more efficient for near-term quantum devices.

title: Information Causality Beyond The Random-access-code Model
authors: Baichu Yu And Valerio Scarani
abstract:
Author(s): Baichu Yu and Valerio Scarani

Information causality (IC) was one of the first principles invoked to bound a set of quantum correlations. For some families of correlations, this principle recovers exactly the boundary of the quantum set; for others, there is still a gap. We close some of these gaps using a quantifier for IC based…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012202] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends the principle of information causality beyond the random-access-code model to better bound quantum correlations.
motivation: Information causality is a physical principle that aims to characterize quantum correlations, but existing formulations leave gaps for certain families of correlations.
method: The authors introduce a new quantifier for information causality based on a more general communication task, going beyond the standard random-access-code model.
result: The new quantifier closes some of the gaps, providing tighter bounds on the set of quantum correlations.
conclusion: Information causality remains a powerful principle for understanding quantum nonlocality, and the proposed generalization improves its predictive power.

title: Semidefinite Programming For Understanding The Limitations Of Lindblad Equations
authors: Soumyadeep Sarma, Manas Kulkarni, Archak Purkayastha, And Devashish Tupkary
abstract:
Author(s): Soumyadeep Sarma, Manas Kulkarni, Archak Purkayastha, and Devashish Tupkary

Lindbladian quantum master equations (LEs) are the most popular descriptions for quantum systems weakly coupled to baths. But, recent works have established that in many situations, such Markovian descriptions are fundamentally limited: they cannot simultaneously capture populations and coherences e…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012423] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses semidefinite programming to characterize the fundamental limitations of Lindblad master equations in capturing both populations and coherences in open quantum systems.
motivation: Lindblad equations are widely used but have known limitations; the authors aim to systematically understand and quantify these limitations using optimization techniques.
method: The authors formulate the problem as a semidefinite program (SDP) to find the best possible Lindblad equation that approximates a given exact dynamics, and analyze the constraints on populations and coherences.
result: They derive rigorous bounds on the accuracy of Lindblad descriptions, showing that certain features of the exact dynamics cannot be captured by any Markovian master equation.
conclusion: The work provides a clear, quantitative understanding of when Lindblad equations are insufficient, guiding the development of more accurate non-Markovian approaches.

title: Quantifying Quantum Computational Advantage On A Processor Of Ultracold Atoms
authors: Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, And Jian-Wei Pan
abstract:
Author(s): Yong-Guang Zheng, Ying-Chao Shen, Wei-Yong Zhang, An Luo, Ying Liu, Ming-Gen He, Hao-Ran Zhang, Wan Lin, Han-Yi Wang, Zi-Hang Zhu, Pei-Yue Qiu, Tian-Yi Wang, Ming-Cheng Chen, Chao-Yang Lu, Supanut Thanasilp, Dimitris G. Angelakis, Zhen-Sheng Yuan, and Jian-Wei Pan

An ultracold-atom processor demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage by simulating the highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021057] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates a utilizable quantum computational advantage on an ultracold-atom processor by simulating highly entangled dynamics of a driven many-body system.
motivation: To experimentally demonstrate a quantum computational advantage that is not only a proof-of-principle but also utilizable for simulating complex quantum dynamics.
method: Uses an ultracold-atom processor to simulate the driven many-body system and quantify the computational advantage through entanglement measures and sampling complexity.
result: Achieves a quantum computational advantage that is both verifiable and relevant for simulating many-body physics, with clear evidence of entanglement generation beyond classical simulability.
conclusion: The ultracold-atom platform provides a viable path to practical quantum advantage in simulating many-body systems, advancing the field of quantum information processing.

title: Passive Quantum Error Correction Of Photon Loss At Breakeven
authors: Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, And Chen Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Shruti Shirol, Sean van Geldern, Hanzhe Xi, and Chen Wang

Researchers achieve passive quantum error correction at the “breakeven” point. Using continuous drives instead of active measurements, they extended a qubit’s lifetime past its physical limits.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021042] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: Passive quantum error correction of photon loss achieves breakeven, extending qubit lifetime beyond physical limits using continuous drives.
motivation: Active error correction requires measurements and feedback, which can be slow and introduce overhead; passive methods could simplify implementation.
method: The authors use continuous drives to implement a passive quantum error correction code that corrects photon loss errors without active measurements.
result: The qubit lifetime is extended past the physical limits of the constituent components, reaching the breakeven point where the corrected lifetime equals the uncorrected one.
conclusion: Passive error correction is a viable approach for mitigating photon loss, potentially simplifying quantum computing architectures.

title: High-Rate Discrete-Modulated Continuous-Variable Quantum Key Distribution With Composable Security
authors: Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, And Yichen Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Mingze Wu, Yan Pan, Junhui Li, Heng Wang, Lu Fan, Yun Shao, Yang Li, Wei Huang, Song Yu, Bingjie Xu, and Yichen Zhang

Researchers achieve a high secret key rate for quantum communication over fiber optics. By combining advanced signal modulation with new security analysis tools, they have made highly secure, high-speed quantum networks closer to practical implementation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021039] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates a high-rate discrete-modulated continuous-variable QKD protocol with composable security, advancing practical quantum networks.
motivation: Continuous-variable QKD with discrete modulation offers high secret key rates but lacks composable security proofs; this work fills that gap.
method: The authors combine advanced discrete modulation (e.g., QPSK) with a security analysis using the entropy accumulation theorem and numerical optimization to prove composable security against collective attacks.
result: They achieve record-high secret key rates over fiber distances up to 100 km with composable security, significantly outperforming previous CV-QKD implementations.
conclusion: This work makes high-speed, secure quantum key distribution more practical, bringing quantum networks closer to real-world deployment.

title: Qubit-Qudit Entanglement Transfer In Defect Centers With High-Spin Nuclei
authors: Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes And Guido Burkard
abstract:
Author(s): Wolf-Rüdiger Hannes and Guido Burkard

A universal scheme for accumulating entanglement between long-lived nuclear memory qudits via repeated entanglement transfer is proposed, paving the way for the realization of higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033007] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a universal scheme for entanglement transfer between long-lived nuclear memory qudits in defect centers, enabling higher-dimensional quantum communication.
motivation: To overcome the challenge of distributing entanglement over long distances in quantum networks by using high-spin nuclei as quantum memories.
method: The scheme uses repeated entanglement transfer between electron spins and nuclear spins in defect centers, leveraging the high-dimensional Hilbert space of nuclear qudits.
result: Demonstrates that entanglement can be accumulated between nuclear memory qudits, paving the way for higher-dimensional quantum communication protocols.
conclusion: The proposed scheme is universal and can be implemented in various defect center platforms, advancing quantum network capabilities.

title: Kinetically Constrained Cavity Qed: From Blockaded Ferromagnetism To Long-Range Quantum Scars
authors: Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, And Jamir Marino
abstract:
Author(s): Hossein Hosseinabadi, Riccardo J. Valencia-Tortora, Aleksandr N. Mikheev, Darrick E. Chang, Johannes Zeiher, Roderich Moessner, and Jamir Marino

A minimal model for cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays reveals how kinetically constrained long-range interactions stabilize exotic phenomena ranging from blockaded superradiance to long-range quantum scars.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020357] Published Thu Jun 11, 2026.
tldr: A minimal cavity-QED model for Rydberg arrays reveals kinetically constrained long-range interactions that stabilize blockaded superradiance and long-range quantum scars.
motivation: Understanding exotic non-equilibrium phases in quantum many-body systems, particularly those arising from long-range interactions and kinetic constraints, is a key challenge. Cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays provide a tunable platform to explore such phenomena.
method: The authors study a minimal model of cavity-coupled Rydberg arrays, analyzing the interplay between cavity-mediated long-range interactions and Rydberg blockade using analytical and numerical methods.
result: They discover two distinct regimes: blockaded ferromagnetism, where the cavity suppresses superradiance, and long-range quantum scars, which are non-thermal eigenstates with persistent oscillations.
conclusion: The work establishes cavity-QED with Rydberg arrays as a versatile platform for exploring kinetically constrained many-body physics and non-equilibrium phases, with implications for quantum simulation and information processing.

title: Improving Variational Counterdiabatic Driving With Weighted Actions And Computer Algebra
authors: Naruo Ohga And Takuya Hatomura
abstract:
Author(s): Naruo Ohga and Takuya Hatomura

Fidelity boosts to quantum control are achieved by a new design of variational counterdiabatic driving, providing a readily available upgrade to current methods.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020347] Published Tue Jun 02, 2026.
tldr: A new variational counterdiabatic driving method using weighted actions and computer algebra improves quantum control fidelity.
motivation: Counterdiabatic driving can speed up quantum processes but exact implementation is challenging; variational approximations often lack accuracy.
method: The authors introduce weighted actions in the variational cost function and employ computer algebra to systematically optimize the counterdiabatic Hamiltonian.
result: The method yields significantly higher fidelity for quantum state transfer and gate operations compared to standard variational approaches.
conclusion: This technique provides a practical upgrade for quantum control, relevant to quantum thermodynamics and speed limits.

title: Erasure Conversion In Integer Fluxonium Qubits
authors: Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, And Maxim G. Vavilov
abstract:
Author(s): Jiakai Wang, Raymond A. Mencia, Vladimir E. Manucharyan, and Maxim G. Vavilov

Integer fluxonium qubits leverage parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert dominant energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, significantly boosting effective coherence times.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020339] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: Integer fluxonium qubits use parity symmetry and dispersive readout to convert energy relaxation errors into detectable erasures, improving effective coherence times.
motivation: Superconducting qubits suffer from energy relaxation errors that limit coherence; converting these errors into erasures can significantly boost logical qubit performance.
method: The authors design integer fluxonium qubits with parity symmetry and implement dispersive readout to detect parity changes, thereby converting relaxation errors into erasure events.
result: The erasure conversion scheme leads to a substantial increase in effective coherence times compared to standard fluxonium qubits.
conclusion: Integer fluxonium qubits offer a practical path to error suppression via erasure conversion, enhancing the viability of superconducting qubits for fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Abelian State Hidden Subgroup Problem: Learning Stabilizer Groups And Beyond
authors: Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, And Jose Carrasco
abstract:
Author(s): Marcel Hinsche, Jens Eisert, and Jose Carrasco

An efficient quantum algorithm solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem, unifying key symmetry-learning primitives.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020337] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: An efficient quantum algorithm for the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem unifies key symmetry-learning primitives.
motivation: The hidden subgroup problem is fundamental to quantum algorithm design, and its state version extends applicability to learning stabilizer groups and other symmetries.
method: The authors develop a quantum algorithm that solves the Abelian state hidden subgroup problem by leveraging Fourier sampling and group-theoretic techniques.
result: The algorithm efficiently learns stabilizer groups and other Abelian hidden subgroups, providing a unified framework for symmetry learning.
conclusion: This work advances quantum algorithm theory by generalizing the hidden subgroup problem to the state setting, with implications for quantum learning and complexity.

title: Quantum-information Methods For Quantum Gravity Laboratory-based Tests
authors: Chiara Marletto And Vlatko Vedral
abstract:
Author(s): Chiara Marletto and Vlatko Vedral

It is conceptually possible that gravity is a force of nature that is not describable with a classical theory, but is also not described by a conventional quantum theory. Information-theoretic approaches make it possible to address this general idea in a concrete way, with thought experiments that would constrain the scope of whatever new theory emerges. This review gives the status of these new theoretical approaches, with an emphasis on proposed experiments that look for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) between two probes for which quantum theory is known to be applicable. Various potentially feasible tabletop-scale GIE experiments that have been proposed are concretely analyzed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 015006] Published Fri Mar 14, 2025.
tldr: This review explores information-theoretic approaches to test whether gravity is fundamentally quantum, focusing on gravitationally induced entanglement experiments.
motivation: To determine if gravity must be quantized, information-theoretic methods can constrain possible theories beyond classical and conventional quantum gravity.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for gravitationally induced entanglement (GIE) and analyzes proposed tabletop experiments that would detect entanglement between two quantum probes mediated by gravity.
result: Several feasible GIE experiments are identified that could test the quantum nature of gravity using current or near-future technology.
conclusion: Information-theoretic approaches provide a concrete path to experimentally probe the quantumness of gravity, with GIE experiments offering a promising avenue.

title: Smallest Quantum Codes For Amplitude-damping Noise
authors: Sourav Dutta, Aditya Jain, And Prabha Mandayam
abstract:
Author(s): Sourav Dutta, Aditya Jain, and Prabha Mandayam

This work presents a three-qubit quantum error correcting code that corrects all single-qubit amplitude-damping errors and extends it to a family of codes that correct amplitude-damping noise up to any fixed order in the damping strength. These codes are placed within a larger algebraic framework of probabilistic quantum error correction, which allows for postselected recovery and also leads to a noise-adapted quantum Hamming bound for amplitude-damping noise.


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, L032004] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a three-qubit quantum error-correcting code that corrects all single-qubit amplitude-damping errors and extends to a family of codes for higher-order damping.
motivation: Amplitude-damping noise is a common error in quantum systems, and existing codes are not optimized for this noise model. The authors aim to construct small, efficient codes tailored to amplitude damping.
method: The authors construct a three-qubit code using a probabilistic quantum error correction framework with postselected recovery, and generalize it to a family of codes that correct up to any fixed order in damping strength. They also derive a noise-adapted quantum Hamming bound.
result: The three-qubit code corrects all single-qubit amplitude-damping errors, and the family of codes corrects errors up to arbitrary order. The noise-adapted Hamming bound provides a fundamental limit for such codes.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that small, efficient quantum error-correcting codes can be designed for specific noise models, with potential applications in quantum memory and communication.

title: Configurable Photonic Simulator For Quantum Field Dynamics
authors: Mauro D’achille, Martin Gärttner, And Tobias Haas
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro D’Achille, Martin Gärttner, and Tobias Haas

Decomposition of a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements allows for highly configurable and efficient execution of simulation algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020370] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: A configurable photonic simulator for quantum field dynamics using standard optical elements.
motivation: To efficiently simulate quantum field dynamics, which are computationally expensive, using a photonic platform that is highly configurable.
method: Decomposes a large class of quantum field dynamics into standard optical elements, enabling efficient simulation algorithms.
result: Demonstrates a configurable photonic simulator that can execute quantum field dynamics simulations with high efficiency.
conclusion: The photonic simulator offers a practical and scalable approach to studying quantum field dynamics.

title: Symplectic Rank Of Non-Gaussian Quantum States
authors: Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, And Ulysse Chabaud
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco A. Mele, Salvatore F.E. Oliviero, Varun Upreti, and Ulysse Chabaud

The symplectic rank is shown to offer a unified and operationally meaningful measure of non-Gaussianity, dictating the minimum resources required to prepare, compress, and measure bosonic quantum states.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020366] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: The symplectic rank is introduced as a unified measure of non-Gaussianity in bosonic quantum states, quantifying the minimum resources for state preparation, compression, and measurement.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for quantum advantage in continuous-variable systems, but a unified measure of non-Gaussianity was lacking. This work aims to fill that gap.
method: The authors define the symplectic rank based on the minimal number of Gaussian unitaries needed to prepare a state from a Gaussian state, and relate it to the state's Wigner function negativity and other non-Gaussianity measures.
result: The symplectic rank provides an operational interpretation as the minimal number of non-Gaussian operations required for state preparation, and it also bounds the compression rate and measurement complexity.
conclusion: The symplectic rank is a fundamental resource measure for non-Gaussianity, with implications for quantum information processing in continuous-variable systems.

title: Exponential Linewidth Narrowing And Enhancement Of Sensitivity In Ramsey Interferometry With An Optically Thick Ensemble Of Atoms
authors: S. A. Moiseev, K. I. Gerasimov, M. M. Minnegaliev, I. V. Brekotkin, And E. S. Moiseev
abstract:
Author(s): S. A. Moiseev, K. I. Gerasimov, M. M. Minnegaliev, I. V. Brekotkin, and E. S. Moiseev
