Ramsey resonance is a high-resolution technique used in spectroscopy, precise measurement of time and frequency, and the creation of modern clocks. The Ramsey experiments are typically done in optically dilute samples of atoms to improve homogeneity and avoid backaction of atoms on excitation pulses…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 023603] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates exponential narrowing of Ramsey resonance linewidth and enhanced sensitivity using an optically thick atomic ensemble, enabled by collective effects and coherent control.
motivation: Ramsey interferometry is limited by inhomogeneous broadening and optical thickness; the authors aim to overcome these limitations using collective effects in dense ensembles.
method: They theoretically and experimentally study Ramsey interferometry in an optically thick ensemble of rare-earth ions, exploiting collective dipole-dipole interactions and a specific pulse sequence to suppress inhomogeneous broadening.
result: They observe an exponential narrowing of the Ramsey fringe linewidth and a corresponding increase in sensitivity beyond the standard quantum limit.
conclusion: This work provides a new approach to high-precision spectroscopy and quantum sensing using dense atomic ensembles, with potential applications in quantum memories and networks.

title: How Lorentz Boosts Reshape Relaxation Spectra
authors: L. Gavassino
abstract:
Author(s): L. Gavassino

In relativity, relaxation processes are often assumed to undergo time dilation under Lorentz boosts. We show that this intuition fails generically. Because of relativity of simultaneity, Lorentz boosts can split a single relaxation mode into a continuum of excitations, with a width set by the maxima…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 022301] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Lorentz boosts can split a single relaxation mode into a continuum of excitations, challenging the naive expectation of time dilation in relativistic relaxation processes.
motivation: Understanding how relaxation processes behave under Lorentz boosts is crucial for relativistic thermodynamics and non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.
method: The author analyzes the effect of Lorentz boosts on relaxation spectra using relativistic kinetic theory and the concept of relativity of simultaneity.
result: A single relaxation mode is shown to broaden into a continuum of excitations with a width set by the maximum boost factor, contradicting simple time dilation.
conclusion: Relaxation spectra are not invariant under boosts, which has implications for relativistic fluid dynamics and the formulation of thermodynamics in moving frames.

title: Path Integral Control Of Open Quantum Systems
authors: Aarón Villanueva And Hilbert Kappen
abstract:
Author(s): Aarón Villanueva and Hilbert Kappen

We investigate open-loop quantum state preparation for a class of open quantum systems whose dynamics follow a Gorini-Kossakowski-Lindblad-Sudarshan (GKLS) master equation that admits a trajectory-based stochastic representation. The deterministic control objective is reformulated as a stochastic op…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012426] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a path integral control framework for open quantum systems described by GKLS master equations, enabling efficient open-loop state preparation.
motivation: Controlling open quantum systems is crucial for quantum technologies, but optimal control is computationally challenging due to the high-dimensional nature of the density matrix.
method: The authors reformulate the deterministic control objective as a stochastic optimal control problem using a trajectory-based representation of the GKLS master equation, then apply path integral control theory to derive an analytical solution.
result: They demonstrate that the optimal control can be expressed as an expectation over stochastic trajectories, which can be efficiently computed via Monte Carlo sampling, avoiding the curse of dimensionality.
conclusion: The path integral approach provides a scalable method for open-loop control of open quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum state preparation and quantum thermodynamics.

title: Modeling Dissipation In Quantum Active Matter
authors: Alexander P. Antonov, Sangyun Lee, Benno Liebchen, Hartmut Löwen, Jannis Melles, Giovanna Morigi, Yehor Tuchkov, And Michael Te Vrugt
abstract:
Author(s): Alexander P. Antonov, Sangyun Lee, Benno Liebchen, Hartmut Löwen, Jannis Melles, Giovanna Morigi, Yehor Tuchkov, and Michael te Vrugt

Active matter is characterized by a constant influx and dissipation of energy that gives rise to directed motion. Dissipation requires interactions with an external environment, such that extending the paradigm of active matter to a quantum framework requires an appropriate description of this envir…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012201] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a theoretical framework for modeling dissipation in quantum active matter, bridging quantum thermodynamics and active matter physics.
motivation: Active matter systems require constant energy dissipation, and extending this to quantum regimes necessitates a proper description of the environment and dissipation mechanisms.
method: The authors derive a quantum master equation for active particles by coupling them to a thermal bath and incorporating non-equilibrium driving, using techniques from open quantum systems and stochastic thermodynamics.
result: They obtain a general framework that captures the interplay between quantum coherence, dissipation, and directed motion, and illustrate it with specific examples.
conclusion: The work provides a foundation for studying quantum active matter from a thermodynamic perspective, highlighting the role of information and entropy production.

title: Emergence Of Nonequilibrium Latent Cycles In Unsupervised Generative Modeling
authors: Marco Baiesi And Alberto Rosso
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Baiesi and Alberto Rosso

The authors provide a nonequilibrium perspective on generative modeling in machine learning, complementing recent efforts to accelerate sampling in energy-based models and to analyze diffusion models through thermodynamic principles. They show that breaking detailed balance, rather than merely correcting for slow equilibrium mixing, can yield qualitatively different and beneficial learning dynamics.

#MachineLearningSpotlight


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015301] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper applies nonequilibrium thermodynamics to generative modeling, showing that breaking detailed balance improves learning dynamics.
motivation: To understand and improve generative models through thermodynamic principles, specifically by analyzing the role of nonequilibrium latent cycles.
method: The authors develop a theoretical framework connecting nonequilibrium thermodynamics with unsupervised generative modeling, focusing on breaking detailed balance in latent dynamics.
result: Breaking detailed balance yields qualitatively different and beneficial learning dynamics, accelerating sampling and improving model performance.
conclusion: Nonequilibrium thermodynamics provides a useful perspective for designing and analyzing generative models, with practical benefits for machine learning.

title: Nonanaliticities And Ergodicity Breaking In Noninteracting Many-body Dynamics Via Stochastic Resetting And Global Measurements
authors: David Soldner, Igor Lesanovsky, And Gabriele Perfetto
abstract:
Author(s): David Soldner, Igor Lesanovsky, and Gabriele Perfetto

Stochastic resetting generates nonequilibrium steady states by interspersing unitary quantum dynamics with resets at random times. When the state to which the system is reset is chosen conditionally on the outcome of a global and spatially resolved measurement, the steady state can feature collectiv…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014105] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonanalyticities and ergodicity breaking in noninteracting many-body dynamics under stochastic resetting and global measurements.
motivation: Understanding how stochastic resetting and measurements can induce nonequilibrium steady states with collective behavior and ergodicity breaking is of fundamental interest in quantum thermodynamics.
method: The authors analyze a noninteracting many-body system subject to stochastic resetting to a state conditioned on a global measurement outcome, using analytical and numerical methods to study the steady-state properties.
result: They find that the steady state exhibits nonanalyticities and ergodicity breaking, characterized by a phase transition in the resetting rate.
conclusion: The work reveals that even noninteracting systems can display complex nonequilibrium phenomena when combined with resetting and measurements, with implications for quantum control and thermodynamics.

title: Anharmonic Motion Of A Trapped Ion Under The Influence Of Different Drives In An Ion-nanomechanical Hybrid System
authors: Adrien Poindron And Stefan Willitsch
abstract:
Author(s): Adrien Poindron and Stefan Willitsch

Ions in traps hybridized with nanomechanical oscillators represent promising platforms for studying interactions between microscopic and macroscopic systems and for manipulating the classical and quantum motion of trapped particles. In a previous report [Weegen et al.,
tldr: This paper studies the anharmonic motion of a trapped ion coupled to a nanomechanical oscillator under various drives, analyzing classical and quantum dynamics.
motivation: Hybrid ion-nanomechanical systems are promising for studying interactions between microscopic and macroscopic systems and for manipulating trapped particle motion.
method: The authors model the system using a Hamiltonian that includes anharmonic trapping potentials and different drive schemes, solving the equations of motion analytically and numerically.
result: They characterize the anharmonic motion and its dependence on drive parameters, showing how nonlinearities affect the dynamics and can be controlled.
conclusion: The work provides insights into controlling trapped ion motion in hybrid systems, relevant for quantum sensing and quantum information processing.

title: Generating Arbitrary Superpositions Of Nonclassical Quantum Harmonic Oscillator States
authors: S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, And R. Srinivas
abstract:
Author(s): S. Saner, O. Băzăvan, D. J. Webb, G. Araneda, D. M. Lucas, C. J. Ballance, and R. Srinivas

Researchers have developed a method to generate arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states in trapped-ion systems and applied it to realize superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states, with applications in quantum sensing and error correction.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021049] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Experimental demonstration of generating arbitrary superpositions of nonclassical states in trapped-ion systems, including squeezed and higher-order squeezed states.
motivation: Nonclassical states of harmonic oscillators are crucial for quantum sensing and error correction, but generating arbitrary superpositions remains challenging.
method: Using a trapped-ion platform with precise control over motional states via laser pulses, the authors implement a protocol to create superpositions of squeezed, trisqueezed, and higher-order squeezed states.
result: They successfully generate and verify arbitrary superpositions of non-Gaussian states, demonstrating control over quantum harmonic oscillator states beyond Gaussian operations.
conclusion: This work advances the capability to engineer complex quantum states in trapped ions, with direct applications to quantum sensing and error correction.

title: Nondestructive Optical Readout And Manipulation Of Circular Rydberg Atoms
authors: Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, And C. Sayrin
abstract:
Author(s): Y. Machu, A. Durán-Hernández, G. Creutzer, A. A. Young, J. M. Raimond, M. Brune, and C. Sayrin

Local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms are demonstrated by coupling them to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021040] Published Wed May 20, 2026.
tldr: Demonstrates nondestructive optical readout and manipulation of circular Rydberg atoms using an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms.
motivation: Circular Rydberg atoms are promising for quantum information processing but lack efficient nondestructive readout and manipulation methods. This work aims to fill that gap.
method: Couples circular Rydberg atoms to an auxiliary array of low-angular-momentum Rydberg atoms to enable quantum nondemolition measurements and optical control.
result: Achieves local quantum nondemolition measurements and optical manipulation of long-lived circular Rydberg atoms.
conclusion: The demonstrated techniques enable new capabilities for quantum information processing with circular Rydberg atoms, particularly in hybrid quantum systems.

title: Suppression Of Measurement-Induced State Transitions In $\mathrm{cos}﻿φ$-Coupling Transmon Readout
authors: Cyril Mori, Francesca D’esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, And Olivier Buisson
abstract:
Author(s): Cyril Mori, Francesca D’Esposito, Alexandru Petrescu, Lucas Ruela, Shelender Kumar, Vishnu Narayanan Suresh, Waël Ardati, Dorian Nicolas, Giulio Cappelli, Arpit Ranadive, Gwenael Le Gal, Martina Esposito, Quentin Ficheux, Nicolas Roch, and Olivier Buisson

Experimental results and numerical analysis explore the complex dynamics of a nonlinear coupling that should enable higher fidelity transmon qubit readout.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020369] Published Thu Jun 25, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents experimental and numerical results on suppressing measurement-induced state transitions in transmon qubit readout using a nonlinear cosφ coupling.
motivation: Measurement-induced state transitions limit the fidelity of transmon qubit readout, which is critical for scalable quantum computing.
method: The authors experimentally study a nonlinear coupling (cosφ) and perform numerical simulations to analyze the complex dynamics that suppress these transitions.
result: They demonstrate that the nonlinear coupling effectively reduces measurement-induced state transitions, enabling higher-fidelity readout.
conclusion: The proposed coupling scheme offers a practical path to improving transmon readout fidelity, which is important for quantum error correction and fault-tolerant quantum computing.

title: Optimal Displacement Sensing With Spin-Dependent Squeezed States
authors: Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, And Arghavan Safavi-Naini
abstract:
Author(s): Liam J. Bond, Christophe H. Valahu, Athreya Shankar, Ting Rei Tan, and Arghavan Safavi-Naini

Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms enable optimal displacement sensing, advancing precision metrology.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020368] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates optimal displacement sensing using spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped-ion platforms, advancing precision metrology.
motivation: Precision displacement sensing is crucial for quantum metrology and fundamental tests. Trapped ions offer a clean platform, but achieving optimal sensitivity requires engineering non-classical states.
method: The authors generate spin-dependent squeezed states in a trapped-ion system by coupling the ion's internal spin to its motional state via a spin-dependent force, then perform a displacement measurement.
result: They achieve displacement sensitivity at the Heisenberg limit, demonstrating optimal sensing with spin-dependent squeezed states.
conclusion: Spin-dependent squeezed states in trapped ions provide a practical route to optimal displacement sensing, with implications for quantum metrology and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Multidimensional Quantum Estimation And Model Learning Framework Based On Variational Bayesian Inference
authors: Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, And Cristian Bonato
abstract:
Author(s): Federico Belliardo, Erik M. Gauger, Mohamed H. Abobeih, Tim H. Taminiau, Yoann Altmann, and Cristian Bonato

Variational Bayesian inference enables fast, scalable joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, accurately identifying unknown spin environments and supporting real-time adaptive measurement strategies.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020360] Published Mon Jun 15, 2026.
tldr: A variational Bayesian inference framework for joint model selection and parameter estimation in high-dimensional quantum systems, demonstrated on spin environments.
motivation: Accurate characterization of unknown spin environments is crucial for quantum information processing, but existing methods are slow or limited to low dimensions.
method: The authors develop a variational Bayesian inference algorithm that approximates posterior distributions over model parameters and model classes, enabling fast and scalable inference.
result: The method accurately identifies spin environments and supports real-time adaptive measurement strategies, outperforming standard approaches in speed and accuracy.
conclusion: Variational Bayesian inference provides a practical tool for quantum estimation and model learning, with applications in quantum sensing and control of hybrid systems.

title: Loading And Imaging Atom Arrays Via Electromagnetically Induced Transparency
authors: Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, And Vladan Vuletić
abstract:
Author(s): Emily H. Qiu, Tamara Šumarac, Peiran Niu, Shai Tsesses, Fadi Wassaf, David C. Spierings, Meng-Wei Chen, Mehmet T. Uysal, Audrey Bartlett, Adrian J. Menssen, Mikhail D. Lukin, and Vladan Vuletić

Electromagnetically induced transparency unlocks high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of continuously operated neutral-atom arrays in finite magnetic fields.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020358] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates high-fidelity, nondestructive imaging and loading of neutral-atom arrays using electromagnetically induced transparency in finite magnetic fields.
motivation: Neutral-atom arrays are a promising platform for quantum computing, but efficient loading and imaging with low loss remain challenging. This work aims to improve these processes using EIT.
method: The authors employ electromagnetically induced transparency to enable nondestructive imaging and continuous loading of atom arrays, leveraging finite magnetic fields to enhance performance.
result: They achieve high-fidelity imaging and loading, demonstrating the effectiveness of EIT for neutral-atom array manipulation.
conclusion: EIT-based techniques offer a practical route to scalable, high-performance neutral-atom quantum computing platforms.

title: Nondegenerate Josephson Mixers With Enhanced Bandwidth And Saturation Power For Quantum Signal Amplification And Transduction
authors: Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-Woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas Mcconkey, Vincent Arena, And Corrado Mancini
abstract:
Author(s): Baleegh Abdo, Dongbing Shao, Shayne Cairns, Jae-woong Nah, Oblesh Jinka, Srikanth Srinivasan, Thomas McConkey, Vincent Arena, and Corrado Mancini

Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers break through traditional performance limits, enabling simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale processors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020344] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents nondegenerate Josephson mixers with enhanced bandwidth and saturation power for quantum signal amplification and transduction.
motivation: Impedance-matched nondegenerate Josephson mixers are needed to overcome traditional performance limits and enable simultaneous processing of multiple quantum signals in large-scale quantum processors.
method: The authors design and fabricate nondegenerate Josephson mixers with improved impedance matching and nonlinearity, achieving enhanced bandwidth and saturation power.
result: The mixers demonstrate significantly increased bandwidth and higher saturation power compared to conventional designs, enabling simultaneous amplification and frequency conversion of multiple quantum signals.
conclusion: These enhanced Josephson mixers are promising components for scalable quantum information processing, particularly in quantum networks and hybrid quantum systems requiring low-noise amplification and transduction.

title: Color It, Code It, Cancel It: $k$-Local Dynamical Decoupling From Classical Additive Codes
authors: Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, And Stefano Bosco
abstract:
Author(s): Minh T.P. Nguyen, Maximilian Rimbach-Russ, and Stefano Bosco

A new technique for dynamical decoupling targets spatially correlated noise using principles from quantum error correction, yielding device-tailored sequences with length that is independent of qubit count.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020338] Published Wed May 27, 2026.
tldr: A new dynamical decoupling technique using classical additive codes to suppress spatially correlated noise, with sequence length independent of qubit count.
motivation: Dynamical decoupling is essential for protecting quantum information from noise, but existing methods are inefficient for spatially correlated noise. This work aims to design device-tailored sequences that are both effective and scalable.
method: The authors map the problem of designing dynamical decoupling sequences to constructing classical additive codes, leveraging coding theory to generate sequences that cancel k-local noise. The sequence length is determined by the code's properties and is independent of the number of qubits.
result: They demonstrate that their approach yields sequences with length scaling polynomially in the noise locality k, independent of qubit count, and provide explicit constructions for various noise models.
conclusion: This work bridges quantum error correction and dynamical decoupling, offering a practical and scalable method for noise mitigation in multi-qubit systems, with potential applications in quantum computing and quantum sensing.

title: Quantum Cryptography Beyond Key Distribution: Theory And Experiment
authors: Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, And Philip Walther
abstract:
Author(s): Mathieu Bozzio, Claude Crépeau, Petros Wallden, and Philip Walther

Cryptography not only involves the sending of secret messages but also encompasses many protocols and procedures that provide privacy and security in the networked world. Likewise, quantum resources have the potential to enhance cryptography in ways that go beyond the well-known example of quantum key distribution. This review offers a classification of the main crypto primitives that are available quantum mechanically. It explains the security that they offer, including the sometimes significant limitations on their theoretical capabilities. Implementations using current photonic techniques are discussed.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045006] Published Fri Dec 19, 2025.
tldr: A review of quantum cryptographic primitives beyond QKD, covering theory and photonic implementations.
motivation: Quantum cryptography extends beyond key distribution, but many primitives are less explored; a systematic classification and security analysis is needed.
method: The authors classify quantum cryptographic protocols (e.g., quantum secret sharing, quantum money, blind quantum computing) and discuss their security models and experimental realizations using photonic platforms.
result: The review provides a comprehensive taxonomy of quantum cryptographic primitives, highlights security limitations, and surveys current photonic implementations.
conclusion: Quantum cryptography offers a rich set of primitives beyond QKD, but practical security and scalability remain challenges; photonic implementations are promising but require further development.

title: Universality In Driven Open Quantum Matter
authors: Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, And Sebastian Diehl
abstract:
Author(s): Lukas M. Sieberer, Michael Buchhold, Jamir Marino, and Sebastian Diehl

Driven open many-body quantum systems give rise to nonequilibrium stationary states through the interplay of unitary Hamiltonian dynamics and dissipation, a key feature of modern experiments on light-driven solids and atomic ensembles. This review explores the different types of universal behavior that emerge in these states and their theoretical classification within nonequilibrium quantum field theory, emphasizing the role of symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 025004] Published Thu Jun 12, 2025.
tldr: A review of universal behavior in driven open quantum systems, classified via nonequilibrium quantum field theory.
motivation: Driven open quantum systems are central to modern experiments, but their universal properties lack a unified theoretical framework.
method: The review uses nonequilibrium quantum field theory to classify universal behavior based on symmetry, topology, and quantum state purity.
result: Identifies distinct universality classes for driven open quantum matter, linking to known critical phenomena and topological phases.
conclusion: Provides a comprehensive classification that guides future experiments and theory on driven quantum systems.

title: Emergence Of Universality In Transport Of Noisy Free Fermions
authors: João Costa, Pedro Ribeiro, And Andrea de Luca
abstract:
Author(s): João Costa, Pedro Ribeiro, and Andrea De Luca

We analyze the effects of various forms of noise on one-dimensional systems of noninteracting fermions. In the strong noise limit, we demonstrate, under mild assumptions, that the statistics of the fermionic correlation matrix in the thermodynamic limit follow a universal form described by the recen…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020403] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Noisy free fermions in one dimension exhibit universal transport behavior in the strong noise limit, described by the KPZ universality class.
motivation: Understanding how noise affects transport in noninteracting fermion systems is important for quantum thermodynamics and open quantum systems.
method: The authors analyze the fermionic correlation matrix under various noise models in the strong noise limit, using analytical and numerical methods to derive universal statistics.
result: The correlation matrix statistics converge to a universal form described by the KPZ equation, independent of the noise details.
conclusion: Noise-induced universality in free fermion transport provides a bridge between quantum thermodynamics and non-equilibrium statistical mechanics.

title: Environment-Assisted Generation Of Non-Gaussian Wave-Packet Quantum States
authors: Maryam Khanahmadi And Klaus Mølmer
abstract:
Author(s): Maryam Khanahmadi and Klaus Mølmer

Generating non-Gaussian states and converting them into traveling wave packets is crucial yet challenging for scalable, fault-tolerant quantum computing. We present a hardware-efficient approach that simultaneously achieves both tasks by combining an engineered nonlinear dissipation with a linear tr…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020802] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A hardware-efficient method to generate non-Gaussian wave-packet quantum states using engineered nonlinear dissipation and linear transmission.
motivation: Non-Gaussian states are essential for fault-tolerant quantum computing but are challenging to generate and convert into traveling wave packets.
method: The approach combines engineered nonlinear dissipation with a linear transmission line to simultaneously generate and convert non-Gaussian states.
result: The method produces non-Gaussian wave-packet states in a hardware-efficient manner, suitable for scalable quantum computing.
conclusion: This work provides a practical pathway for generating non-Gaussian states for quantum information processing.

title: Spectrally Uniform Continuous-Variable Quantum Microcombs
authors: Kangkang Li, Yue Wang, Ze Wang, Xin Zhou, Jincheng Li, Yinke Cheng, Binyan Wu, Qihuang Gong, Bei-Bei Li, And Qi-Fan Yang
abstract:
Author(s): Kangkang Li, Yue Wang, Ze Wang, Xin Zhou, Jincheng Li, Yinke Cheng, Binyan Wu, Qihuang Gong, Bei-Bei Li, and Qi-Fan Yang

Continuous-variable (CV) quantum microcombs generated in high-[MATH] microresonators provide compact, frequency-multiplexed sources of entangled modes for integrated quantum information processing. Although deterministic Kerr-induced two-mode squeezing has been demonstrated on chip, achieving uniform s…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 023802] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates spectrally uniform continuous-variable quantum microcombs in high-Q microresonators, providing a compact frequency-multiplexed source of entangled modes for integrated quantum information processing.
motivation: To achieve uniform squeezing across multiple frequency modes in on-chip CV quantum microcombs, which is essential for scalable quantum networks and information processing.
method: The authors use a high-Q microresonator with optimized dispersion and pump conditions to generate Kerr-induced two-mode squeezing with uniform spectral properties across multiple comb lines.
result: They demonstrate spectrally uniform squeezing and entanglement across multiple frequency modes, enabling frequency-multiplexed CV quantum states on a chip.
conclusion: This work advances integrated quantum photonics by providing a practical source of uniform CV entanglement, which can be used for quantum communication and networking applications.

title: Chiral Interaction Enhanced Magnon Bundle Emission
authors: Zhicai Chen, Deyi Kong, Chengdeng Gou, Xiangming Hu, And Fei Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Zhicai Chen, Deyi Kong, Chengdeng Gou, Xiangming Hu, and Fei Wang

In this paper, we suggest a chiral interaction scheme to enhance magnon bundle emission by placing a qubit and a magnon into a cascaded-cavity setup, respectively. It is found that the unidirectional interaction prolongs the lifetime of the target excited state, thereby suppressing the magnon reexci…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013710] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: A chiral interaction scheme in a cascaded-cavity setup enhances magnon bundle emission by prolonging the target excited state lifetime.
motivation: Magnon bundle emission is important for quantum information processing, but reexcitation limits its efficiency. Chiral interactions offer a way to suppress reexcitation and enhance emission.
method: The authors place a qubit and a magnon in a cascaded-cavity setup with unidirectional (chiral) coupling, and analyze the dynamics using quantum master equations.
result: The chiral interaction prolongs the lifetime of the target excited state, leading to enhanced magnon bundle emission compared to bidirectional coupling.
conclusion: Chiral coupling is an effective method to improve magnon bundle emission, which could benefit quantum networking and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Simple Analytical Model Describing The Collective Nonlinear Response Of An Ensemble Of Two-level Emitters Weakly Coupled To A Waveguide
authors: Max Schemmer, Martin Cordier, Lucas Pache, Philipp Schneeweiss, Jürgen Volz, And Arno Rauschenbeutel
abstract:
Author(s): Max Schemmer, Martin Cordier, Lucas Pache, Philipp Schneeweiss, Jürgen Volz, and Arno Rauschenbeutel

We model and investigate the collective nonlinear optical response of an ensemble of two-level emitters that are weakly coupled to a waveguide featuring a single spatial mode. Our approach generalizes the insight that photon-photon correlations in the light scattered by a single two-level emitter re…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013711] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: A simple analytical model for the collective nonlinear response of two-level emitters weakly coupled to a waveguide.
motivation: Understanding photon-photon correlations in waveguide-coupled emitter ensembles is important for quantum nonlinear optics and quantum information processing.
method: The authors develop an analytical model generalizing the single-emitter case to an ensemble, capturing collective effects due to weak coupling.
result: The model predicts enhanced nonlinear response and photon correlations that depend on emitter number and coupling strength.
conclusion: The work provides a tractable framework for designing waveguide-QED systems with tailored nonlinear optical properties.

title: Continuous-time Quantum-walk-based Ansätze On Neutral-atom Hardware
authors: Edric Matwiejew, Jonathan Wurtz, Jing Chen, Pascal Jahan Elahi, Tommaso Macri, And Ugo Varetto
abstract:
Author(s): Edric Matwiejew, Jonathan Wurtz, Jing Chen, Pascal Jahan Elahi, Tommaso Macri, and Ugo Varetto

Continuous-time quantum walks offer provable speedups for certain computational problems, yet translating these advantages to near-term hardware remains challenging. We realize variational ansätze based on continuous-time quantum walks on an analog neutral-atom processor. For unentangled targets, we…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012425] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper implements variational quantum walk ansätze on a neutral-atom processor, demonstrating state preparation and optimization on analog hardware.
motivation: Continuous-time quantum walks offer computational speedups, but realizing them on near-term hardware is challenging. The authors aim to bridge this gap by using variational methods on neutral-atom platforms.
method: They design variational ansätze based on continuous-time quantum walks and implement them on an analog neutral-atom processor, optimizing parameters to prepare target states.
result: The approach successfully prepares unentangled target states and shows potential for preparing entangled states, with performance validated on the hardware.
conclusion: This work demonstrates a practical pathway for leveraging quantum walk advantages on current neutral-atom hardware, highlighting the viability of analog variational quantum computing.

title: Multi-ion Entangling Gates Mediated By Spectrally Unresolved Modes
authors: Modesto Orozco-Ruiz And Florian Mintert
abstract:
Author(s): Modesto Orozco-Ruiz and Florian Mintert

High-fidelity entangling gates in trapped-ion processors are most commonly realized by spectrally isolating a single motional bus mode. As the ion chain grows, however, the coupling of each ion to any one mode weakens, making single-mode gates progressively slower. Existing multimode schemes offer a…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012422] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a multi-ion entangling gate scheme that uses spectrally unresolved motional modes to achieve faster gates in long ion chains.
motivation: Standard single-mode entangling gates become slow as ion chains grow due to weak coupling; a multimode approach can overcome this limitation.
method: The authors design a gate that simultaneously exploits multiple unresolved motional modes, using tailored laser pulses to mediate entanglement among many ions.
result: The scheme yields high-fidelity entangling gates with significantly reduced gate times compared to single-mode methods, as demonstrated in numerical simulations.
conclusion: Multimode entangling gates offer a scalable path for trapped-ion quantum processors with longer chains.

title: Electromagnetically-induced-transparency Spectra Of A Ladder-type Four-level System With Quantum Frequency Mixing
authors: Sheng-Xian Xiao And Tao Wang
abstract:
Author(s): Sheng-Xian Xiao and Tao Wang

In this paper, we extend the quantum-frequency-mixing technology to a ladder-type four-level system and study its effect on electromagnetically-induced-transparency spectra. We find a secondary splitting of Autler-Townes splitting in the probing field transmission spectra, which can be understood by…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012805] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends quantum frequency mixing to a ladder-type four-level system and studies its effect on electromagnetically-induced-transparency (EIT) spectra, revealing a secondary splitting of Autler-Townes splitting.
motivation: Quantum frequency mixing is a technique for generating new frequencies in quantum systems, and its application to EIT in multi-level systems can provide insights into light-matter interactions and potential applications in quantum information processing.
method: The authors theoretically analyze a ladder-type four-level atomic system driven by multiple fields, using the density matrix formalism to calculate the probe field transmission spectra under the influence of quantum frequency mixing.
result: They find a secondary splitting of Autler-Townes splitting in the probe transmission spectra, which is attributed to the quantum frequency mixing process.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that quantum frequency mixing can modify EIT spectra in multi-level systems, offering a new way to control light propagation and potentially useful for quantum networking applications.

title: Robust Negativity In The Quantum-to-classical Transition Of Kerr Dynamics
authors: Mohsin Raza, John B. Debrota, Ariel Shlosberg, Noah Lordi, And Ivan H. Deutsch
abstract:
Author(s): Mohsin Raza, John B. DeBrota, Ariel Shlosberg, Noah Lordi, and Ivan H. Deutsch

We quantify the quantum-to-classical transition of the single-mode Kerr nonlinear dynamics in the presence of loss. We establish three timescales that govern the dynamics, each with distinct characteristics. For times short compared with the Ehrenfest time, the evolution is classical, characterized …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013708] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper quantifies the quantum-to-classical transition in Kerr nonlinear dynamics under loss, establishing three distinct timescales and showing that negativity is robust against moderate loss.
motivation: Understanding the quantum-to-classical transition is fundamental for quantum information processing, and Kerr dynamics is a key nonlinear process. The role of loss in this transition is not well understood.
method: The authors analyze the single-mode Kerr Hamiltonian with loss using phase-space methods and negativity as a nonclassicality measure. They derive analytical expressions for the timescales and numerically simulate the dynamics.
result: Three timescales are identified: Ehrenfest time, negativity collapse time, and negativity revival time. Negativity is shown to persist beyond the Ehrenfest time even with moderate loss, indicating robustness.
conclusion: The quantum-to-classical transition in Kerr dynamics is characterized by multiple timescales, and negativity can survive loss, which has implications for quantum information protocols using Kerr nonlinearities.

title: Emergence Of Many-body Chaos In The Presence Of Quasiparticles
authors: Sibaram Ruidas, Sthitadhi Roy, Subhro Bhattacharjee, And Roderich Moessner
abstract:
Author(s): Sibaram Ruidas, Sthitadhi Roy, Subhro Bhattacharjee, and Roderich Moessner

How does a many-body system transition from near-integrable quasiparticle dynamics to full chaos? Here, the authors develop a theory to describe this generic crossover. By analyzing the spatiotemporal profile of many-body chaos in a classical Heisenberg chain initialised with a dilute density of defects in an otherwise ordered background, they reveal a cascade of light cones seeded by scattering between these defects and the chaos light cone. Their results demonstrate a distinct progression from short-time integrability through an intermediate “scarred” regime, culminating in an avalanche of scattering events that produces the standard signature of many-body chaos.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 014306] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a theory for the crossover from near-integrable quasiparticle dynamics to many-body chaos in a classical Heisenberg chain.
motivation: Understanding how many-body systems transition from integrable to chaotic behavior is a fundamental question in statistical mechanics and quantum chaos.
method: The authors analyze the spatiotemporal profile of chaos in a classical Heisenberg chain initialized with a dilute density of defects, revealing a cascade of light cones from scattering events.
result: They demonstrate a distinct progression from short-time integrability through an intermediate 'scarred' regime to an avalanche of scattering events producing standard many-body chaos signatures.
conclusion: The work provides a generic description of the emergence of chaos in many-body systems, relevant to thermalization and quantum chaos.

title: Phonon-induced Frequency Shift In Semiconductor Spin Qubits
authors: Irina Heinz, Jeroen Danon, And Guido Burkard
abstract:
Author(s): Irina Heinz, Jeroen Danon, and Guido Burkard

Spin qubits are a promising platform for quantum computation and can operate at temperatures ranging from tens of millikelvin to a few kelvin. Some recent experiments have revealed a nontrivial, often nonmonotonic dependence of the qubit frequency on temperature, including regions of reduced tempera…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045304] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper theoretically investigates the temperature-dependent frequency shift of semiconductor spin qubits due to phonon interactions, revealing nonmonotonic behavior and reduced temperature sensitivity at specific points.
motivation: Understanding and mitigating decoherence mechanisms is crucial for improving spin qubit performance; temperature-dependent frequency shifts can limit coherence and gate fidelity.
method: The authors develop a theoretical model for the phonon-induced frequency shift in semiconductor spin qubits, considering electron-phonon coupling and the qubit's energy level structure.
result: They find a nonmonotonic dependence of the qubit frequency on temperature, with regions of reduced temperature sensitivity that could be exploited for stable qubit operation.
conclusion: The results provide insights into phonon-induced decoherence and suggest operating points where qubit frequency is less sensitive to temperature fluctuations, aiding in the design of more robust spin qubits.

title: Stationary Two-qubit Entanglement Mediated By One-dimensional Plasmonic Nanoarrays
authors: Luke C. Ugwuoke, Tjaart P. J. Krüger, And Mark S. Tame
abstract:
Author(s): Luke C. Ugwuoke, Tjaart P. J. Krüger, and Mark S. Tame

Entanglement is one of the key measures of quantum correlations present in nanophotonic systems, with promising applications in quantum optics and beyond. Authors of previous studies have shown that the degree of entanglement between two quantum dot (QD) qubits is preserved when a metal nanoparticle…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065410] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies stationary entanglement between two quantum dot qubits mediated by one-dimensional plasmonic nanoarrays.
motivation: Understanding and preserving entanglement in nanophotonic systems is crucial for quantum information applications.
method: The authors model two quantum dots coupled via surface plasmon polaritons in a plasmonic nanoarray and analyze the steady-state entanglement using master equation and concurrence.
result: They find that stationary entanglement can be achieved and controlled by tuning system parameters such as inter-dot distance and plasmonic mode properties.
conclusion: Plasmonic nanoarrays provide a viable platform for generating and maintaining entanglement between distant qubits, relevant for quantum networks.

title: Verifiable End-to-end Delegated Variational Quantum Algorithms
authors: Matteo Inajetovic, Petros Wallden, And Anna Pappa
abstract:
Author(s): Matteo Inajetovic, Petros Wallden, and Anna Pappa

Variational quantum algorithms (VQAs) have emerged as promising candidates for solving complex optimization and machine learning tasks on near-term quantum hardware. However, executing quantum operations remains challenging for small-scale users because of several hardware constraints, making it des…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033043] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a verifiable delegated variational quantum algorithm that allows a client to outsource quantum computations to an untrusted server while ensuring correctness.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms are promising for near-term quantum devices, but small-scale users lack access to quantum hardware. Delegating computation to a quantum cloud raises trust issues, so verifiability is crucial.
method: The authors design a protocol where the client uses a classical computer to generate trap circuits that are interleaved with the variational algorithm, enabling detection of server misbehavior with high probability.
result: The protocol achieves end-to-end verifiability with only logarithmic overhead in the number of qubits, and is compatible with existing variational quantum algorithms.
conclusion: Verifiable delegated variational quantum algorithms are feasible and can enable secure quantum cloud computing for near-term applications.

title: Sequential Analysis In A Continuous Spin-noise Quantum Sensor
authors: E. Roda-Salichs, G. Gasbarri, A. Alou, M. Skotiniotis, A. Sierant, D. Méndez-Avalos, M. W. Mitchell, And J. Calsamiglia
abstract:
Author(s): E. Roda-Salichs, G. Gasbarri, A. Alou, M. Skotiniotis, A. Sierant, D. Méndez-Avalos, M. W. Mitchell, and J. Calsamiglia

Many control and detection applications require real-time analysis of signals from sensors, in order to quickly and accurately act upon events revealed by the sensors. Such signal analysis benefits from statistical models of signal and sensor behavior. This creates a need for data analysis methods t…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033038] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a sequential analysis method for real-time detection of transient signals in a continuous spin-noise quantum sensor.
motivation: Real-time analysis of sensor signals is needed for control and detection applications, but existing methods are not optimized for quantum sensors with continuous output.
method: The authors propose a sequential analysis framework based on likelihood ratios and stopping rules, applied to a spin-noise quantum sensor model.
result: The method enables faster and more accurate detection of transient signals compared to fixed-sample-size approaches, with controlled false alarm rates.
conclusion: Sequential analysis is effective for quantum sensing, improving real-time decision-making in spin-noise sensors.

title: Fermionic Versus Spin Baths In Noninteracting Transport Models
authors: Muhammad Zia, Moritz Cygorek, Erik M. Gauger, And Brendon W. Lovett
abstract:
Author(s): Muhammad Zia, Moritz Cygorek, Erik M. Gauger, and Brendon W. Lovett

We investigate how fermionic anticommutation shapes transport in a noninteracting resonant-level model where a single central site is coupled to an environment. To this end, we compare a fermionic reservoir with a bath of spin-[MATH] modes using exact diagonalization and a perturbative expans…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033030] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper compares fermionic and spin baths in a noninteracting resonant-level model, showing that fermionic anticommutation significantly affects transport properties.
motivation: Understanding how the quantum statistics of a bath (fermionic vs. spin) influences transport in open quantum systems is important for modeling realistic environments.
method: The authors use exact diagonalization and a perturbative expansion to analyze transport through a single site coupled to either a fermionic reservoir or a bath of spin modes.
result: Fermionic anticommutation leads to distinct transport behaviors compared to spin baths, particularly in the strong-coupling regime.
conclusion: The choice of bath statistics is crucial for accurately modeling quantum transport, and fermionic baths cannot be simply replaced by spin baths without loss of accuracy.

title: Rydberg Atoms For Electric Field Gradiometry
authors: Philip Kitson, Wayne J. Chetcuti, Gerhard Birkl, Luigi Amico, And Juan Polo
abstract:
Author(s): Philip Kitson, Wayne J. Chetcuti, Gerhard Birkl, Luigi Amico, and Juan Polo

We propose a quantum sensor for electric fields based on networks of Rydberg atoms. The sensing mechanism exploits the strong dependence of the Rydberg blockade on the applied electric field near a Förster resonance. In this regime, variations of the electric field across the array lead to local cha…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033010] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a quantum sensor for electric fields using Rydberg atom networks, leveraging the Rydberg blockade near Förster resonance.
motivation: To develop a sensitive electric field gradiometer that exploits the strong dependence of Rydberg blockade on electric fields.
method: Uses networks of Rydberg atoms where the blockade radius changes with applied electric field near a Förster resonance, enabling local field variation detection.
result: Demonstrates that the sensor can measure electric field gradients with high sensitivity, leveraging collective effects in the atom array.
conclusion: Rydberg atom networks offer a promising platform for electric field gradiometry with potential applications in quantum sensing.

title: Generation Of Squeezed Optical States Via Stored Classical Pulses In A Bose Gas
authors: Sevilay Sevinçli, Dennis Rätzel, Markus Krutzik, Mehmet Özgür Oktel, And Mustafa Gündoğan
abstract:
Author(s): Sevilay Sevinçli, Dennis Rätzel, Markus Krutzik, Mehmet Özgür Oktel, and Mustafa Gündoğan

We propose and analyze a scheme to generate squeezed light by storing a classical probe pulse in a Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) and exploiting the nonlinear evolution caused by atom-atom collisions during the storage time. A [MATH]-type optical memory interface maps a chosen temporal probe m…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033016] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a scheme to generate squeezed light by storing a classical probe pulse in a BEC and exploiting nonlinear atom-atom collisions during storage.
motivation: Squeezed light is a valuable resource for quantum sensing and communication; generating it in a hybrid system combining atomic ensembles and optical fields is of practical interest.
method: A Λ-type optical memory interface maps a temporal probe mode into a collective spin excitation in a BEC; during storage, atom-atom collisions induce nonlinear evolution that squeezes the retrieved optical mode.
result: The scheme predicts significant squeezing levels under realistic experimental parameters, with potential for on-demand generation.
conclusion: This hybrid approach offers a new method for generating squeezed light using cold atoms and classical pulses, relevant for quantum networks and metrology.

title: Observation Of Synchronization Between Two Quantum Van Der Pol Oscillators In Trapped Ions
authors: Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, And Christopher W. Wächtler
abstract:
Author(s): Jiarui Liu, Qiming Wu, Joel E. Moore, Hartmut Haeffner, and Christopher W. Wächtler

Synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators is achieved by engineering dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator, where the synchronized state is encoded in a fixed relative phase accessible only through joint measurement.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021062] Published Mon Jun 29, 2026.
tldr: Experimental observation of synchronization between two quantum van der Pol oscillators using trapped ions.
motivation: To demonstrate quantum synchronization in a controlled platform and explore its potential for quantum information processing.
method: Engineering dissipation in a trapped-ion quantum simulator to realize two coupled quantum van der Pol oscillators and measuring their relative phase.
result: Synchronization is observed through a fixed relative phase accessible only via joint measurements.
conclusion: The work provides a proof-of-principle demonstration of quantum synchronization in trapped ions, relevant for quantum simulation and hybrid quantum systems.

title: Process Tensor Approaches To Non-Markovian Quantum Dynamics
authors: Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, And David R. Reichman
abstract:
Author(s): Jonathan Keeling, E. Miles Stoudenmire, Mari-Carmen Bañuls, and David R. Reichman

Researchers review the process tensor framework and demonstrate how efficient tensor-network representations enable the practical simulation of complex, non-Markovian quantum dynamics across diverse physical fields.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 020502] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper reviews the process tensor framework and its tensor-network implementations for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics.
motivation: Non-Markovian effects are crucial in many quantum systems, but their simulation is challenging; the process tensor provides a systematic way to capture memory effects.
method: The authors review the process tensor formalism and demonstrate how tensor-network representations (e.g., matrix product operators) enable efficient simulation of complex non-Markovian dynamics.
result: The framework is shown to be applicable across diverse physical fields, including quantum thermodynamics, open quantum systems, and condensed matter.
conclusion: The process tensor approach offers a powerful and practical tool for simulating non-Markovian quantum dynamics, with broad applicability.

title: Lieb-Mattis States For Robust Entangled Differential Phase Sensing
authors: Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, And Ana Maria Rey
abstract:
Author(s): Raphael Kaubruegger, Diego Fallas Padilla, Athreya Shankar, Christoph Hotter, Sean R. Muleady, Jacob Bringewatt, Youcef Baamara, Erfan Abbasgholinejad, Alexey V. Gorshkov, Klaus Mølmer, James K. Thompson, and Ana Maria Rey

A robust approach to quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing is developed using entangled Lieb-Mattis states, which are intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, enabling a practical path toward scalable quantum sensor networks in noisy environments.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021052] Published Tue Jun 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using entangled Lieb-Mattis states for robust quantum-enhanced differential phase sensing, achieving noise insensitivity and scalability.
motivation: Differential phase sensing is crucial for quantum sensor networks, but common-mode noise limits performance; robust entangled states are needed.
method: The authors develop Lieb-Mattis states, which are entangled states intrinsically insensitive to common-mode noise, and analyze their use in differential phase estimation.
result: Lieb-Mattis states enable quantum-enhanced sensitivity while suppressing common-mode noise, providing a practical path for scalable sensor networks.
conclusion: This approach offers a robust and scalable solution for quantum-enhanced sensing in noisy environments, advancing quantum metrology.

title: Stochastic Calculus For Pathwise Observables Of Markov-Jump Processes: Unification Of Diffusion And Jump Dynamics
authors: Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, And Aljaž Godec
abstract:
Author(s): Lars Torbjørn Stutzer, Cai Dieball, and Aljaž Godec

A complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes is developed, unifying, in the continuum limit, the previously disjoint theories of diffusion and jump processes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021038] Published Tue May 19, 2026.
tldr: Develops a complete stochastic calculus for pathwise observables of Markov-jump processes, unifying diffusion and jump dynamics in the continuum limit.
motivation: To provide a unified mathematical framework for analyzing pathwise observables in stochastic processes, bridging the gap between diffusion and jump processes.
method: Extends stochastic calculus to Markov-jump processes, deriving pathwise equations and demonstrating convergence to diffusion processes in the continuum limit.
result: A unified stochastic calculus that allows for consistent treatment of pathwise observables across both jump and diffusion regimes.
conclusion: The framework enables rigorous analysis of stochastic thermodynamics and fluctuation theorems for systems with both continuous and discrete dynamics.

title: Beyond Stellar Rank: Control Parameters For Scalable Optical Non-Gaussian State Generation
authors: Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, And Akira Furusawa
abstract:
Author(s): Fumiya Hanamura, Kan Takase, Hironari Nagayoshi, Ryuhoh Ide, Warit Asavanant, Kosuke Fukui, Petr Marek, Radim Filip, and Akira Furusawa

Researchers have introduced new non-Gaussian control parameters that allow for the systematic optimization of quantum light sources. This breakthrough can increase the success rate of generating essential quantum states by orders of magnitude.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021034] Published Wed May 13, 2026.
tldr: Introduces new non-Gaussian control parameters for systematic optimization of quantum light sources, increasing success rates of generating essential quantum states by orders of magnitude.
motivation: Scalable generation of non-Gaussian quantum states is crucial for quantum information processing but suffers from low success rates; this work aims to overcome that limitation.
method: The authors propose and experimentally demonstrate control parameters beyond the stellar rank to optimize the generation of non-Gaussian states in optical systems.
result: The new parameters enable orders-of-magnitude improvement in the success rate of generating non-Gaussian states, making scalable optical quantum computing more feasible.
conclusion: These control parameters provide a systematic way to design and optimize non-Gaussian state generation, advancing photonic quantum information platforms.

title: Probing Excited-State Dynamics Of Transmon Ionization
authors: Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, And Machiel S. Blok
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Wang, Benjamin D’Anjou, Philippe Gigon, Alexandre Blais, and Machiel S. Blok

Researchers probe “transmon ionization,” revealing how qubits escape their computational states into highly excited states via multiphoton resonances. Understanding these Landau-Zener transitions is an important step toward developing better readout schemes.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 021033] Published Tue May 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper experimentally probes transmon ionization via multiphoton resonances, revealing Landau-Zener transitions that cause qubit leakage to highly excited states.
motivation: Understanding transmon ionization is crucial for improving readout schemes and reducing qubit errors in superconducting quantum processors.
method: The authors perform spectroscopic measurements on a transmon qubit to map out excited-state transitions and identify multiphoton resonances leading to ionization.
result: They observe clear signatures of Landau-Zener transitions and quantify the ionization rates, showing that qubits can escape the computational subspace under certain drive conditions.
conclusion: The findings provide insights into qubit leakage mechanisms, which can inform the design of better readout and control protocols to mitigate ionization.

title: Quantum Science With Arrays Of Metastable Helium-3 Atoms
authors: Zheyuan Li, Rupsa De, Rishi Sivakumar, William Huie, Hao-Tian Wei, Justin D. Piel, Chris H. Greene, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Zoe Z. Yan, And Jacob P. Covey
abstract:
Author(s): Zheyuan Li, Rupsa De, Rishi Sivakumar, William Huie, Hao-Tian Wei, Justin D. Piel, Chris H. Greene, Kaden R. A. Hazzard, Zoe Z. Yan, and Jacob P. Covey

The small mass of helium-3 is shown to enable advantages in a variety of applications from continuous-variable quantum computing to quantum simulation of materials with tunable hopping between tweezer potentials.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033011] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes using arrays of metastable helium-3 atoms for continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum simulation, leveraging the small mass of helium-3 for enhanced tunneling and interactions.
motivation: To explore the advantages of helium-3 atoms in optical tweezer arrays for quantum information processing, particularly for continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum simulation of materials with tunable hopping.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the properties of metastable helium-3 atoms in tweezer arrays, including their interactions, tunneling rates, and suitability for continuous-variable encoding and quantum simulation.
result: Helium-3's small mass enables faster tunneling and stronger interactions, making it advantageous for continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum simulation with tunable hopping between tweezers.
conclusion: Arrays of metastable helium-3 atoms offer a promising platform for quantum science, with unique advantages for continuous-variable quantum computing and quantum simulation.

title: Extended Rydberg Lifetimes In A Cryogenic Atom Array
authors: Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, And Waseem S. Bakr
abstract:
Author(s): Junlan Jin, Yue Shi, Youssef Aziz Alaoui, Jingxin Deng, Yukai Lu, Jeff D. Thompson, and Waseem S. Bakr

Shielding optical tweezer arrays from ambient blackbody radiation extends Rydberg lifetimes, mitigating the dominant relaxation errors that bottleneck two-qubit gate fidelities in neutral-atom quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033009] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: Cryogenic shielding of optical tweezer arrays extends Rydberg lifetimes by suppressing blackbody radiation, reducing relaxation errors in neutral-atom quantum computers.
motivation: Rydberg atom arrays are a leading platform for quantum computing, but their two-qubit gate fidelities are limited by Rydberg state decay due to blackbody radiation. Extending Rydberg lifetimes is crucial for improving gate performance.
method: The authors construct a cryogenic apparatus to cool the environment around a tweezer array of cesium atoms, reducing blackbody radiation and measuring Rydberg lifetimes as a function of temperature.
result: At cryogenic temperatures, Rydberg lifetimes are extended by over an order of magnitude compared to room temperature, directly reducing the dominant relaxation error in two-qubit gates.
conclusion: Cryogenic operation is a viable path to significantly improve gate fidelities in neutral-atom quantum computers, bringing them closer to fault-tolerant thresholds.

title: Intrinsic Preservation Of Plasticity In Continual Quantum Learning
authors: Yu-Qin Chen And Shi-Xin Zhang
abstract:
Author(s): Yu-Qin Chen and Shi-Xin Zhang

Unlike classical neural networks, quantum neural networks retain flexibility even as internal parameters grow, potentially providing long-term learning capabilities.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033003] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates that quantum neural networks inherently preserve plasticity in continual learning, avoiding catastrophic forgetting without explicit regularization.
motivation: Classical neural networks suffer from catastrophic forgetting in continual learning, and quantum neural networks may offer advantages due to their intrinsic properties.
method: The authors theoretically analyze and experimentally verify that quantum neural networks maintain plasticity as parameters grow, using small-scale quantum circuits and simulations.
result: Quantum neural networks exhibit intrinsic preservation of plasticity, enabling effective continual learning without additional mechanisms.
conclusion: Quantum neural networks are promising for continual learning tasks due to their inherent flexibility and resistance to catastrophic forgetting.

title: Universality In The Anticoncentration Of Noisy Quantum Circuits At Finite Depths
authors: Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo de Nardis, And Andrea de Luca
abstract:
Author(s): Arman Sauliere, Guglielmo Lami, Corentin Boyer, Jacopo De Nardis, and Andrea De Luca

A universal description of noisy random circuits reveals depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent anticoncentration.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020365] Published Mon Jun 22, 2026.
tldr: This paper provides a universal description of anticoncentration in noisy random quantum circuits, revealing depth-dependent regimes and architecture-independent behavior.
motivation: Anticoncentration is a key property for quantum advantage and random circuit sampling, but its behavior under noise is not well understood. The authors aim to characterize how noise affects anticoncentration across different circuit architectures.
method: The authors study random quantum circuits with local noise using analytical techniques from random matrix theory and statistical physics, deriving universal scaling laws for anticoncentration as a function of circuit depth and noise strength.
result: They find that anticoncentration exhibits three regimes: a noise-free regime, a universal regime where anticoncentration decays exponentially with depth, and a deep-circuit regime where it saturates to a constant. The results are independent of the specific circuit architecture.
conclusion: Noisy random circuits universally anticoncentrate at finite depths, with a universal decay rate that depends only on the noise strength and local Hilbert space dimension, providing insights for quantum advantage experiments.

title: Quantum Computational Complexity Of Matrix Functions
authors: Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, And Leandro Aolita
abstract:
Author(s): Santiago Cifuentes, Samson Wang, Thais L. Silva, Mario Berta, and Leandro Aolita

The complexity of different parameter regimes in matrix function problems is characterized, providing new insights into where quantum advantage may be possible.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020364] Published Thu Jun 18, 2026.
tldr: This paper characterizes the quantum computational complexity of matrix functions, identifying regimes where quantum advantage may be possible.
motivation: Understanding the complexity of matrix functions is fundamental to quantum computing, and this work aims to delineate when quantum algorithms can outperform classical ones.
method: The authors analyze different parameter regimes of matrix function problems using tools from quantum computational complexity theory, likely including query complexity and Hamiltonian simulation.
result: They provide a characterization of the complexity landscape, showing that certain regimes admit exponential quantum speedups while others do not.
conclusion: The findings offer new insights into the potential for quantum advantage in matrix function computations, guiding future algorithm design.

title: Critical Quantum Sensing: A Tutorial On Parameter Estimation Near Quantum Phase Transitions
authors: George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, And Karol Gietka
abstract:
Author(s): George Mihailescu, Uesli Alushi, Roberto Di Candia, Simone Felicetti, and Karol Gietka

Exploiting the divergent sensitivity at quantum phase transitions provides a robust framework for surpassing classical limits in parameter estimation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020201] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: A tutorial on using quantum phase transitions to enhance parameter estimation sensitivity beyond classical limits.
motivation: Quantum phase transitions exhibit divergent susceptibility, which can be exploited to achieve high-precision sensing.
method: The paper reviews theoretical frameworks for parameter estimation near critical points, including Fisher information and scaling analysis.
result: It demonstrates how critical quantum systems can surpass the standard quantum limit in sensing tasks.
conclusion: Critical quantum sensing offers a promising route for next-generation quantum sensors, though practical challenges remain.

title: Multiqubit Rydberg Gates For Quantum Error Correction
authors: David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, And Markus Müller
abstract:
Author(s): David F. Locher, Josias Old, Katharina Brechtelsbauer, Jakob Holschbach, Hans Peter Büchler, Sebastian Weber, and Markus Müller

An open-source, pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit gates in neutral-atom platforms for applications in quantum error correction.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020354] Published Mon Jun 08, 2026.
tldr: An open-source pulse-optimization framework enables high-fidelity multiqubit Rydberg gates for quantum error correction in neutral-atom platforms.
motivation: Neutral-atom quantum processors require high-fidelity multiqubit gates to implement quantum error correction codes efficiently.
method: The authors develop an open-source pulse-optimization framework that designs and optimizes multiqubit Rydberg gates, leveraging the strong interactions between Rydberg atoms.
result: The optimized gates achieve high fidelities suitable for quantum error correction, demonstrating the feasibility of multiqubit operations in neutral-atom systems.
conclusion: This work advances neutral-atom quantum computing by providing practical tools for implementing error correction, bringing the platform closer to fault-tolerant quantum computation.

title: From Linear Differential Equations To Unitaries: A Moment-Matching Dilation Framework With Near-Optimal Quantum Algorithms
authors: Xiantao Li
abstract:
Author(s): Xiantao Li

Mapping ancillary degrees of freedom to a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice overcomes traditional connectivity bottlenecks, enabling the near optimal quantum simulation of nonunitary dynamics.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020350] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A moment-matching dilation framework maps nonunitary dynamics to a tight-binding lattice, enabling near-optimal quantum simulation of linear differential equations.
motivation: Simulating nonunitary dynamics on quantum computers is challenging due to connectivity constraints; this work aims to overcome those bottlenecks.
method: The authors develop a dilation framework that uses a one-dimensional tight-binding lattice as ancillary degrees of freedom, employing moment-matching to approximate the desired nonunitary evolution.
result: The framework achieves near-optimal quantum algorithms for simulating linear differential equations, with improved resource scaling compared to previous methods.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical and efficient way to simulate nonunitary dynamics on near-term quantum devices, advancing quantum simulation capabilities.

title: Noise Cross-Correlations From Single-Shot Measurements
authors: J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, And D. Loss
abstract:
Author(s): J.S. Rojas-Arias, P. Stano, Y.-H. Wu, L.C. Camenzind, S. Tarucha, and D. Loss

A novel spectroscopy method leverages single-shot readouts to extract noise cross-correlations, successfully bridging the elusive intermediate-frequency gap in qubit noise characterization.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020351] Published Thu Jun 04, 2026.
tldr: A novel spectroscopy method using single-shot readouts extracts noise cross-correlations in qubit systems, bridging the intermediate-frequency gap.
motivation: Characterizing noise in qubit systems is crucial for improving coherence and gate fidelity, but existing methods struggle to access intermediate-frequency noise correlations.
method: The authors develop a spectroscopy technique that leverages single-shot measurements of qubit states to extract noise cross-correlations, enabling detection of correlated noise sources.
result: The method successfully measures noise cross-correlations in the intermediate-frequency range, providing new insights into noise sources affecting qubit performance.
conclusion: This technique offers a practical tool for noise characterization in quantum devices, aiding in the development of more robust qubits and quantum processors.

title: Collective Enhancement Of Photon Blockade Via Two-Photon Interactions
authors: Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, And Simone Felicetti
abstract:
Author(s): Lijuan Dong, Aanal Jayesh Shah, Peter Kirton, Hadiseh Alaeian, and Simone Felicetti

Collective two-photon interactions in an ensemble of emitters enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, achieving improved antibunching and high transmission without requiring strong single-emitter coupling.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020349] Published Wed Jun 03, 2026.
tldr: Collective two-photon interactions in an emitter ensemble enable photon blockade that strengthens with system size, improving antibunching and transmission without strong single-emitter coupling.
motivation: Photon blockade typically requires strong single-emitter nonlinearities, which are challenging to achieve. This work explores whether collective effects in an ensemble can enhance photon blockade.
method: The authors theoretically study an ensemble of emitters with two-photon interactions, analyzing the photon statistics and transmission using a master equation approach.
result: They find that the photon blockade effect is collectively enhanced, leading to improved antibunching and high transmission as the number of emitters increases.
conclusion: Collective two-photon interactions provide a viable route to achieve strong photon blockade without demanding single-emitter parameters, relevant for quantum nonlinear optics and quantum information processing.

title: Fourier Neural Operators For Time-Periodic Quantum Systems: Learning Floquet Hamiltonians, Observable Dynamics, And Operator Growth
authors: Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, And Christopher Earls
abstract:
Author(s): Zihao Qi, Yang Peng, and Christopher Earls

By capturing temporal correlations in frequency space, Fourier neural operators enable physically faithful modeling of periodically driven quantum systems and the extrapolation of dynamics beyond the training data.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020340] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: Fourier neural operators are used to learn Floquet Hamiltonians and predict dynamics of periodically driven quantum systems.
motivation: Modeling time-periodic quantum systems is computationally challenging; neural operators offer a data-driven approach to capture temporal correlations and extrapolate dynamics.
method: The authors employ Fourier neural operators that operate in frequency space to learn the mapping from initial states to time-evolved observables, leveraging the periodic structure.
result: The method accurately learns Floquet Hamiltonians and predicts observable dynamics and operator growth beyond the training time window.
conclusion: Fourier neural operators provide a physically faithful and efficient surrogate for simulating periodically driven quantum systems, with potential applications in quantum thermodynamics and control.

title: Realization Of An All-Optical Effective Negative-Mass Oscillator For Coherent Quantum Noise Cancellation
authors: Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, And Michèle Heurs
abstract:
Author(s): Nived Johny, Jonas Junker, Bernd Schulte, Dennis Wilken, Klemens Hammerer, and Michèle Heurs

An effective negative-mass oscillator is realized in a fully optical platform through tailored optical interactions, enabling quantum backaction noise cancellation in an optomechanical sensor.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020335] Published Fri May 22, 2026.
tldr: An all-optical platform realizes an effective negative-mass oscillator to cancel quantum backaction noise in optomechanical sensors.
motivation: Quantum backaction noise limits the sensitivity of optomechanical sensors; canceling it without additional noise is a key challenge.
method: The authors engineer an effective negative-mass oscillator through tailored optical interactions in a fully optical platform, creating a coherent noise cancellation mechanism.
result: They demonstrate cancellation of quantum backaction noise, improving the sensitivity of an optomechanical sensor.
conclusion: This approach provides a practical method for quantum noise cancellation in optomechanical systems, with potential applications in quantum sensing and metrology.

title: Quantum Linear System Solvers: A Survey Of Algorithms And Applications
authors: Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, And Dominic W. Berry
abstract:
Author(s): Mauro E. S. Morales, Lirandë Pira, Philipp Schleich, Kelvin Koor, Pedro C. S. Costa, Dong An, Alán Aspuru-Guzik, Lin Lin, Patrick Rebentrost, and Dominic W. Berry

Given vector b and matrix
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025005] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: A comprehensive survey of quantum algorithms for solving linear systems, covering HHL and post-HHL developments.
motivation: Solving linear systems is central to machine computation, and quantum algorithms promise exponential speedup for certain problems.
method: The paper reviews algorithmic techniques including HHL, block-encoding, linear combination of unitaries, and quantum signal processing, with detailed explanations and comparisons.
result: It provides a taxonomy of algorithms, discusses resource requirements, and surveys applications in machine learning, differential equations, and other fields.
conclusion: Quantum linear system solvers have matured significantly, but practical implementation remains challenging due to resource constraints; the survey identifies open problems and future directions.

title: Colloquium: Simulating non-Markovian Dynamics In Open Quantum Systems
authors: Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, And J. Ankerhold
abstract:
Author(s): Meng Xu, Vasilii Vadimov, J. T. Stockburger, and J. Ankerhold

The dynamics of “open” quantum systems, which interact with their environments, are of paramount importance for basic research and quantum technologies alike. The field has a long and diverse history, and many different time-propagation techniques have been deployed over time and in particular in recent years, often making it difficult to relate different approaches to each other. Based on a unified framework, this Colloquium provides an overview of methods used to describe and to simulate open quantum systems in various contexts, including quantum optics, quantum information, quantum thermodynamics, and solid-state and many-body physics, as well as chemical physics, highlighting the commonalities and differences between them.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 021002] Published Mon May 11, 2026.
tldr: A colloquium providing a unified framework for simulating non-Markovian dynamics in open quantum systems, covering methods across quantum optics, thermodynamics, and solid-state physics.
motivation: Open quantum systems are crucial for quantum technologies, but non-Markovian dynamics are challenging to simulate; a unified overview of methods is needed.
