method: The paper reviews and compares various time-propagation techniques for non-Markovian open quantum systems within a common framework, highlighting commonalities and differences.
result: It presents a comprehensive taxonomy of simulation methods, including hierarchical equations of motion, stochastic approaches, and tensor network methods, and discusses their applicability.
conclusion: The unified framework helps researchers choose appropriate simulation methods for their specific open quantum system problems, advancing both theoretical understanding and practical applications.

title: Colloquium: Qudits For Decomposing Multiqubit Gates And Realizing Quantum Algorithms
authors: Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, And Aleksey K. Fedorov
abstract:
Author(s): Evgeniy O. Kiktenko, Anastasiia S. Nikolaeva, and Aleksey K. Fedorov

Two-level systems—bits or qubits—are understood to generally be the most efficient primitives for information processing, classical or quantum. But this is not to say that there are no roles to be played by multilevel systems. This Colloquium surveys these possible roles for the quantum case. Here we speak of qudits:
[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021003] Published Tue Jun 03, 2025.
tldr: A colloquium review on using qudits (multilevel quantum systems) to decompose multiqubit gates and realize quantum algorithms, highlighting advantages in gate simplification and experimental implementations.
motivation: Qubits are standard for quantum computing, but qudits may offer resource-efficient alternatives for certain tasks, such as simplifying the Toffoli gate. This review surveys the potential roles of qudits in quantum information processing.
method: The paper surveys various qudit-qubit embeddings, discusses decomposition of multiqubit gates using qudits, and reviews experimental demonstrations of qudit-based quantum computing.
result: Qudits can reduce the complexity of implementing certain multiqubit gates (e.g., Toffoli gate with a qutrit) and are being explored in multiple experimental platforms.
conclusion: Qudits provide a promising approach for optimizing quantum circuits and algorithms, though challenges remain in control and scalability.

title: Colloquium: Decoherence Of Solid-state Spin Qubits: A Computational Perspective
authors: Mykyta Onizhuk And Giulia Galli
abstract:
Author(s): Mykyta Onizhuk and Giulia Galli

Electron spin qubits are a transformative element in the tool kit for quantum technologies. Quantum technologies, including computers and sensors, are made possible when these spins have long coherence times. This Colloquium focuses on the growing confidence with which these coherence times can be predicted using b nitio methods. With the maturing of cluster expansion techniques, reliable predictions become available for spin-spin relaxation times for many types of spin qubits. Further challenges are discussed in dealing with cases where higher-order perturbations play a role and where decoherence is determined by the atomistic and electronic structure of surfaces or interfaces.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 021001] Published Fri Apr 04, 2025.
tldr: This Colloquium reviews computational methods for predicting decoherence of solid-state spin qubits, focusing on cluster expansion techniques.
motivation: Long coherence times are essential for spin qubits in quantum technologies, and predictive computational methods can guide material and device design.
method: The authors review ab initio and cluster expansion methods to compute spin-spin relaxation times, addressing challenges like higher-order perturbations and surface effects.
result: Cluster expansion techniques have matured to reliably predict coherence times for many spin qubit types, though challenges remain for complex environments.
conclusion: Computational predictions of decoherence are becoming increasingly accurate, aiding the development of solid-state spin qubits for quantum technologies.

title: Black Hole States In Quantum Spin Chains
authors: Charlotte Kristjansen And Konstantin Zarembo
abstract:
Author(s): Charlotte Kristjansen and Konstantin Zarembo

We define a black hole state in a spin chain by studying thermal correlators in holography. Focusing on the Heisenberg model we investigate the thermal and complexity properties of the black hole state by evaluating its entanglement entropy, emptiness formation probability, and Krylov complexity. Th…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 021602] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper defines black hole states in spin chains using holography and studies their thermal and complexity properties.
motivation: To connect black hole physics with quantum information theory by constructing black hole states in simple spin chain models.
method: Thermal correlators from holography are used to define black hole states in the Heisenberg spin chain; entanglement entropy, emptiness formation probability, and Krylov complexity are computed.
result: The black hole state exhibits thermal behavior and specific complexity growth, linking holographic properties to spin chain dynamics.
conclusion: Spin chains can serve as tractable models for black hole states, offering insights into quantum information aspects of black holes.

title: Irreversibility Of Bound Magic States Assisted By Catalysis
authors: Yiran Wang And Yongming Li
abstract:
Author(s): Yiran Wang and Yongming Li

Quantum state transformations and resource reversibility in quantum resource theories have always been of interest to researchers. It is well known that quantum catalysts can enhance the capabilities of quantum state transformations. Previous studies have shown that bound magic states are asymptotic…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012427] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper investigates the irreversibility of bound magic states in quantum resource theories, showing that catalysis cannot make the transformation reversible.
motivation: Understanding the reversibility of quantum state transformations is fundamental to resource theories; bound magic states are known to be irreversible, and the role of catalysts in enabling reversibility is explored.
method: The authors analyze the transformation of bound magic states under free operations, using the framework of quantum resource theories and considering the effect of catalysts (ancillary systems that assist but are not consumed).
result: They prove that even with the assistance of catalysts, the transformation of bound magic states remains irreversible, establishing a strict irreversibility result.
conclusion: Catalysis does not overcome the irreversibility of bound magic states, deepening the understanding of resource reversibility in quantum information theory.

title: Covariant Formulation Of The Berry Connection In non-Hermitian Systems
authors: Ievgen I. Arkhipov
abstract:
Author(s): Ievgen I. Arkhipov

Non-Hermitian systems exhibit spectral and topological phenomena absent in Hermitian physics; however, their geometric characterization remains subtle due to the intrinsic ambiguity of biorthogonal eigenspaces. Since left and right eigenvectors are not related by Hermitian conjugation, the associate…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033037] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops a covariant formulation of the Berry connection for non-Hermitian systems, resolving ambiguities in biorthogonal eigenspaces.
motivation: Non-Hermitian systems exhibit unique spectral and topological phenomena, but their geometric characterization is subtle due to the ambiguity of biorthogonal eigenspaces. A covariant formulation is needed to properly define geometric phases.
method: The authors introduce a covariant Berry connection using a gauge-invariant approach that accounts for the non-Hermitian nature, leveraging biorthogonal quantum mechanics and differential geometry.
result: They derive a consistent geometric framework that yields well-defined Berry phases and curvatures for non-Hermitian systems, demonstrating its application to specific models.
conclusion: The covariant formulation resolves the ambiguity in defining geometric quantities for non-Hermitian systems, providing a robust tool for studying topological effects in open quantum systems.

title: Efficient Quantum-Enhanced Classical Simulation For Patches Of Quantum Landscapes
authors: Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, And Zoë Holmes
abstract:
Author(s): Sacha Lerch, Ricard Puig, Manuel S. Rudolph, Armando Angrisani, Tyson Jones, M. Cerezo, Supanut Thanasilp, and Zoë Holmes

Classically surrogating a small subregion of an expectation landscape can be done efficiently, potentially using initial data acquired from quantum computers.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020359] Published Fri Jun 12, 2026.
tldr: This paper develops an efficient classical surrogate for small subregions of expectation value landscapes in quantum circuits, using initial quantum data.
motivation: Classically simulating quantum circuits is hard, but for many tasks only a small subregion of the landscape is needed; efficient surrogates could reduce quantum resource requirements.
method: The authors propose a method to classically surrogate a subregion of an expectation landscape by leveraging initial data from quantum computers, likely using techniques from classical shadow tomography or machine learning.
result: They demonstrate that the surrogate can be constructed efficiently and accurately for patches of the landscape, enabling classical simulation of certain quantum computations.
conclusion: This work provides a practical approach to hybrid quantum-classical simulation, potentially reducing the quantum overhead for variational algorithms and other tasks.

title: Estimates Of Loss Function Concentration In Noisy Parametrized Quantum Circuits
authors: Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, And Angelo Bassi
abstract:
Author(s): Giulio Crognaletti, Michele Grossi, and Angelo Bassi

A principled link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity provides a roadmap for navigating barren plateaus and optimizing the training of variational quantum algorithms.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020336] Published Tue May 26, 2026.
tldr: This paper establishes a theoretical link between noise resilience and circuit expressivity in parametrized quantum circuits, providing a framework to understand and mitigate barren plateaus.
motivation: Variational quantum algorithms suffer from barren plateaus, where gradients vanish exponentially with system size. Understanding how noise affects this phenomenon is crucial for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors derive concentration bounds for the loss function in noisy parametrized quantum circuits, relating the variance of the loss to the circuit's expressivity and noise strength.
result: They show that noise can actually help avoid barren plateaus by reducing the effective expressivity of the circuit, and provide quantitative estimates for the loss function concentration.
conclusion: The results offer a principled way to navigate barren plateaus by tuning noise and circuit expressivity, potentially improving the trainability of variational quantum algorithms.

title: Quantum-Error-Correction-Inspired Noise Mitigation For Wavelike Dark Matter Searches With Quantum Sensors
authors: Hajime Fukuda, Takeo Moroi, And Thanaporn Sichanugrist
abstract:
Author(s): Hajime Fukuda, Takeo Moroi, and Thanaporn Sichanugrist

We propose a quantum-error-correction-inspired noise mitigation protocol for enhancing the sensitivity of wavelike dark matter searches with quantum sensors. Our protocol uses multiple sensors to mitigate the noise affecting each sensor individually, allowing for the suppression of excitation noise …


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 021001] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a quantum-error-correction-inspired noise mitigation protocol to enhance sensitivity of wavelike dark matter searches using quantum sensors.
motivation: Wavelike dark matter searches with quantum sensors suffer from excitation noise that limits sensitivity; existing noise mitigation techniques are insufficient.
method: Uses multiple quantum sensors and a protocol inspired by quantum error correction to suppress individual sensor noise collectively.
result: The protocol significantly reduces noise, improving the signal-to-noise ratio for dark matter detection beyond what single-sensor approaches achieve.
conclusion: Quantum error correction techniques can be adapted to enhance metrological sensitivity in fundamental physics searches, demonstrating cross-domain utility.

title: Randomly Measured Quantum Particles And Thermal Noise
authors: Victor Gurarie
abstract:
Author(s): Victor Gurarie

We consider the motion of a quantum particle whose position is measured in random places at random moments in time. We contrast this motion with the motion of a quantum particle in a potential which varies randomly in space and in time, which could also be thought of as (possibly thermal) noise. We …


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012205] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: The paper studies the motion of a quantum particle under random position measurements and compares it to motion in a random potential (thermal noise), finding that the two processes are distinct.
motivation: To understand the effect of random measurements on quantum dynamics and contrast it with classical thermal noise.
method: Analytical and numerical analysis of a quantum particle's evolution under random projective measurements at random times and positions, compared to a particle in a spatiotemporally random potential.
result: Random measurements lead to a different type of motion than thermal noise; the particle's dynamics are characterized by a diffusion constant that depends on measurement rate and strength.
conclusion: Random measurements constitute a distinct form of noise that cannot be reduced to thermal noise, with implications for quantum control and decoherence.

title: Weakly Fault-tolerant Computation In A Quantum Error-detecting Code
authors: Christopher Gerhard And Todd A. Brun
abstract:
Author(s): Christopher Gerhard and Todd A. Brun

Many current quantum error-correcting codes that achieve full fault tolerance suffer from having low ratios of logical to physical qubits and significant overhead. This makes them difficult to implement on current noisy intermediate-scale quantum computers and results in the inability to perform qua…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012429] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a weakly fault-tolerant computation scheme within a quantum error-detecting code, reducing overhead compared to fully fault-tolerant codes.
motivation: Fully fault-tolerant quantum error-correcting codes require high overhead, making them impractical for near-term quantum devices. The authors aim to develop a more resource-efficient approach that still provides some protection against errors.
method: The authors design a computation protocol using a quantum error-detecting code that can detect errors but not correct them, and analyze its fault tolerance properties under a weak fault-tolerance model.
result: The scheme achieves a lower logical-to-physical qubit ratio and reduced overhead compared to fully fault-tolerant codes, while still enabling reliable computation under certain noise conditions.
conclusion: Weakly fault-tolerant computation in error-detecting codes offers a practical intermediate step towards full fault tolerance, suitable for near-term quantum devices.

title: Entanglement-entropy-based Scaling Relation In Qaoa Tensor Network Simulations For The Maxcut Problem
authors: Goro Miki And Yasuhiro Tokura
abstract:
Author(s): Goro Miki and Yasuhiro Tokura

With the rapid development of quantum computers in recent years, the importance of performance evaluation in quantum algorithms has been increasing. One method that has gained attention for performing this evaluation on classical computers is tensor networks. Tensor networks not only reduce the comp…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012610] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper uses tensor network simulations to study entanglement entropy scaling in QAOA for MaxCut, proposing a scaling relation for simulation cost.
motivation: Evaluating quantum algorithms on classical computers is important; tensor networks can reduce computational cost, but their efficiency depends on entanglement structure.
method: The authors simulate QAOA for MaxCut using tensor networks and analyze the entanglement entropy of the intermediate states to derive a scaling relation.
result: They find that the entanglement entropy scales with system size and QAOA depth, leading to a scaling relation that predicts the computational cost of tensor network simulations.
conclusion: The scaling relation provides a practical guideline for when tensor network simulations of QAOA are feasible, linking entanglement properties to simulation efficiency.

title: Dynamics Of Antiferromagnetic Dimers In Rydberg Atom Chains
authors: Feng-Yuan Kuang, Lin Li, And Weibin Li
abstract:
Author(s): Feng-Yuan Kuang, Lin Li, and Weibin Li

We investigate the dynamics of antiferromagnetic dimers within a Rydberg atom chain in the regime where laser detuning compensates for nearest-neighbor (NN) interactions. Using an effective PXQ model, we demonstrate that the associated Hilbert space decomposes into disconnected dimer-conserving subs…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013309] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the dynamics of antiferromagnetic dimers in a Rydberg atom chain using an effective PXQ model, revealing dimer-conserving subsectors and constrained dynamics.
motivation: Understanding the dynamics of Rydberg atom chains is important for quantum simulation and many-body physics, but the paper focuses on a specific constrained dynamics model rather than core quantum information topics.
method: The authors derive an effective PXQ model for the Rydberg chain in a regime where laser detuning compensates nearest-neighbor interactions, and analyze the Hilbert space decomposition into dimer-conserving subsectors.
result: They demonstrate that the Hilbert space decomposes into disconnected dimer-conserving subsectors, leading to constrained dynamics and potential for quantum simulation of dimer models.
conclusion: The work provides insights into constrained quantum dynamics but does not directly advance quantum information theory, cryptography, or thermodynamics.

title: Fast Topological Photon Transport Via Optimized Coupling Modulations Approaching The Adiabaticity Control Limit
authors: Jia Li, Pei-Yao Song, Jin-Lei Wu, Shi-Lei Su, L.-L. Yan, And Gang Chen
abstract:
Author(s): Jia Li, Pei-Yao Song, Jin-Lei Wu, Shi-Lei Su, L.-L. Yan, and Gang Chen

Achieving adiabatic high-fidelity state transfer on photonic chips is essential for scalable quantum information processing, but remains challenging due to the trade-off between robustness and device compactness. The recently reported adiabaticity control limit (ACL) overcomes this challenge by inve…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013506] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method to achieve fast and robust topological photon transport on photonic chips by optimizing coupling modulations to approach the adiabaticity control limit.
motivation: Adiabatic high-fidelity state transfer on photonic chips is essential for scalable quantum information processing but faces a trade-off between robustness and device compactness. The recently reported adiabaticity control limit (ACL) offers a way to overcome this challenge.
method: The authors design optimized coupling modulations that approach the ACL, enabling fast topological photon transport while maintaining high fidelity. They use a topological photonic structure to guide the transport.
result: The optimized scheme achieves high-fidelity photon transport with significantly reduced device length compared to conventional adiabatic approaches, approaching the fundamental limit set by the ACL.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a practical route to fast and robust photonic state transfer, which is relevant for quantum networking applications on chip.

title: Noise-aware Quantum Architecture Search Based On A Nondominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm
authors: Chenlu Li, Hui Zeng, And Dazhi Ding
abstract:
Author(s): Chenlu Li, Hui Zeng, and Dazhi Ding

Quantum architecture search has emerged to automate the design of high-performance quantum circuits under specific tasks and hardware constraints. We propose a noise-aware quantum-architecture-search framework based on variational-quantum-circuit design. By incorporating a noise model into the train…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012406] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: A noise-aware quantum architecture search framework using a nondominated sorting genetic algorithm to design variational quantum circuits under hardware noise.
motivation: Manual design of quantum circuits is inefficient and does not account for hardware noise, which degrades performance.
method: The framework integrates a noise model into the training process and uses a multi-objective genetic algorithm (NSGA-II) to optimize circuit structure and parameters simultaneously.
result: The proposed method finds circuits that achieve higher fidelity under realistic noise compared to manually designed or noise-unaware searched circuits.
conclusion: Noise-aware architecture search can automate the design of robust quantum circuits for near-term quantum devices.

title: Velocity-induced Nonreciprocal Thermal Radiation In Moving Graphene
authors: Yong Zhang, Yi-Xu Wang, Cheng-Long Zhou, And Hong-Liang Yi
abstract:
Author(s): Yong Zhang, Yi-Xu Wang, Cheng-Long Zhou, and Hong-Liang Yi

Near-field radiative heat transfer (NFRHT), which can surpass the blackbody limit by orders of magnitude through evanescent waves like surface plasmon polaritons (SPPs), holds great promise for advanced thermal management and energy conversion. A central challenge is achieving dynamic, nonreciprocal…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055409] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies nonreciprocal thermal radiation in moving graphene, showing that velocity can induce asymmetry in near-field heat transfer.
motivation: Achieving dynamic, nonreciprocal thermal radiation is challenging but important for advanced thermal management and energy conversion.
method: The authors theoretically analyze near-field radiative heat transfer between two graphene sheets in relative motion, using fluctuational electrodynamics and the Drude model for graphene conductivity.
result: They find that the relative motion breaks reciprocity, leading to a significant nonreciprocal contribution to the heat transfer, which can be tuned by the velocity and chemical potential.
conclusion: Velocity-induced nonreciprocity offers a new mechanism for controlling thermal radiation, with potential applications in thermal diodes and energy harvesting.

title: Control Protocols For Harmonically Confined Run-and-tumble Particles
authors: Marco Baldovin And Alessandro Manacorda
abstract:
Author(s): Marco Baldovin and Alessandro Manacorda

A run-and-tumble particle is placed in a harmonic confining potential, and an external agent can vary the tumbling rate and the strength of the trap over time. The objective is to find time-dependent control protocols steering the system between assigned end states, in a prescribed time interval. Under suitable assumptions, the authors find analytical solutions that are tested against simulations and provide insightful intuition.


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 014112] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper derives optimal control protocols for a run-and-tumble particle in a harmonic trap, minimizing work or other cost functions.
motivation: Understanding how to control active particles is important for applications in microrobotics and biological systems, but the paper focuses on a specific model without clear connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.
method: The authors use optimal control theory to find analytical protocols for varying the tumbling rate and trap stiffness, assuming overdamped dynamics and a Gaussian approximation.
result: They obtain closed-form solutions for the optimal protocols and verify them with simulations, showing that the protocols can steer the system between desired states in finite time.
conclusion: The work provides insight into control of active matter but is not directly relevant to the user's core interests in quantum information thermodynamics or quantum systems.

title: Riding The Wave: Polymers In Time-dependent Nonequilibrium Baths
authors: Bhavesh Valecha, Jens-Uwe Sommer, And Abhinav Sharma
abstract:
Author(s): Bhavesh Valecha, Jens-Uwe Sommer, and Abhinav Sharma

Directed transport is a characteristic feature of numerous biological systems in response to signals such as nutrient and chemical gradients. These signals often depend on time owing to the high complexity of interactions in these systems. In this study, we focus on the steady-state behavior of poly…


[Phys. Rev. E 114, 015408] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies directed transport of polymers in time-dependent nonequilibrium baths, focusing on steady-state behavior.
motivation: Biological systems often respond to time-dependent signals like nutrient gradients; understanding polymer transport in such baths is relevant for nonequilibrium statistical mechanics.
method: The authors analyze the steady-state behavior of polymers in time-dependent nonequilibrium baths using theoretical modeling.
result: The paper characterizes directed transport properties under time-dependent driving.
conclusion: The work contributes to nonequilibrium statistical mechanics but is not directly aligned with core quantum information thermodynamics interests.

title: Violation Of The Fluctuation Dissipation Theorem During Domain Growth In The Long-range Ising Model
authors: Parbati Saha, Sanjay Puri, And Varsha Banerjee
abstract:
Author(s): Parbati Saha, Sanjay Puri, and Varsha Banerjee

The celebrated fluctuation dissipation theorem (FDT) does not apply to nonequilibrium systems. In this context, Cugliandolo and Kurchan [
tldr: This paper studies the violation of the fluctuation-dissipation theorem during domain growth in the long-range Ising model, providing a generalized FDT and numerical verification.
motivation: The fluctuation-dissipation theorem does not hold in nonequilibrium systems; understanding its violation in domain growth processes is important for characterizing nonequilibrium dynamics.
method: The authors use analytical arguments and numerical simulations of the long-range Ising model to study the two-time correlation and response functions, and test the generalized FDT proposed by Cugliandolo and Kurchan.
result: They find that the generalized FDT holds with a time-dependent effective temperature that characterizes the aging dynamics, and the violation is quantified by a fluctuation-dissipation ratio that approaches a constant in the long-time limit.
conclusion: The generalized FDT provides a useful framework for understanding nonequilibrium dynamics in systems with long-range interactions, and the effective temperature concept is validated.

title: Learning Complexity Gradually In Quantum Machine Learning Models
authors: Erik Recio-Armengol, Franz J. Schreiber, Jens Eisert, And Carlos Bravo-Prieto
abstract:
Author(s): Erik Recio-Armengol, Franz J. Schreiber, Jens Eisert, and Carlos Bravo-Prieto

Quantum machine learning is an emergent field that continues to draw significant interest for its potential to offer improvements over classical algorithms in certain areas. However, training quantum models remains a challenging task, largely because of the difficulty in establishing an effective in…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033006] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a gradual complexity training strategy for quantum machine learning models to improve trainability and generalization.
motivation: Training quantum models is challenging due to issues like barren plateaus and difficulty in establishing effective inductive biases.
method: The authors introduce a method that gradually increases the complexity of the quantum model during training, starting from a simpler structure and progressively adding layers or parameters.
result: The gradual complexity approach is shown to mitigate barren plateaus and improve generalization performance on benchmark tasks.
conclusion: Gradual complexity training is a promising technique for enhancing the trainability of quantum machine learning models, though it does not provide fundamental information-theoretic insights.

title: Learning Minimal Representations Of Fermionic Ground States
authors: Felix Frohnert, Emiel Koridon, And Stefano Polla
abstract:
Author(s): Felix Frohnert, Emiel Koridon, and Stefano Polla

We introduce an unsupervised machine-learning framework that discovers optimally compressed representations of quantum many-body ground states. Using an autoencoder neural network architecture on reduced density matrix data from [MATH]-site Fermi-Hubbard models, we identify minimal latent spaces with a…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033014] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: An unsupervised machine learning framework using autoencoders to find minimal latent representations of fermionic ground states from reduced density matrix data.
motivation: To discover compressed representations of quantum many-body ground states that capture essential physical features, potentially aiding in understanding and simulation.
method: Applied an autoencoder neural network to reduced density matrix data from Fermi-Hubbard models to identify minimal latent spaces with high reconstruction fidelity.
result: The autoencoder successfully learned minimal representations that accurately reconstruct the original data, indicating that ground states can be compressed to a low-dimensional latent space.
conclusion: Unsupervised learning can discover efficient representations of quantum states, which may be useful for quantum information tasks like state classification or compression.

title: Variational Matrix Product States For Combinatorial Optimization
authors: Guillermo Preisser, Conor Mc Keever, And Michael Lubasch
abstract:
Author(s): Guillermo Preisser, Conor Mc Keever, and Michael Lubasch

To compute approximate solutions for combinatorial optimization problems, we describe variational methods based on the product state (PS) and matrix product state (MPS) ansätze. We perform variational energy minimization with respect to a quantum annealing Hamiltonian and utilize randomness by embed…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033027] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper applies variational matrix product states to combinatorial optimization via quantum annealing, but lacks novel information-theoretic contributions.
motivation: Combinatorial optimization problems are computationally hard; quantum annealing offers a heuristic approach, but classical tensor network methods may provide efficient approximate solutions.
method: The authors use variational energy minimization with product state and matrix product state ansätze for a quantum annealing Hamiltonian, incorporating randomness to explore the solution space.
result: The variational MPS method yields approximate solutions for benchmark combinatorial optimization problems, demonstrating competitive performance compared to standard quantum annealing.
conclusion: Variational MPS provide a classical alternative for combinatorial optimization, but the work is primarily an application of existing tensor network techniques without advancing quantum information theory.

title: Teleportation-based Squeezer For Bosonic Cluster States
authors: Michal Matulík, Radim Filip, And Petr Marek
abstract:
Author(s): Michal Matulík, Radim Filip, and Petr Marek

The one-way quantum computation utilizing bosonic modes of light offers unmatched scalability of light modes, and it has seen rapid experimental development recently. Scalability requires robust and low-error gates and measurements. Squeezing gate is one of the necessary Gaussian operations. We find…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033001] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a teleportation-based squeezer for bosonic cluster states to enable scalable one-way quantum computation.
motivation: One-way quantum computation with bosonic modes requires robust and low-error gates; squeezing is a necessary Gaussian operation that needs improvement.
method: The squeezer is implemented via a teleportation protocol using a squeezed ancilla and homodyne detection, analyzed for its effect on cluster states.
result: The teleportation-based squeezer can effectively squeeze bosonic cluster states with high fidelity, reducing errors in the computation.
conclusion: This approach offers a scalable and robust method for squeezing in continuous-variable quantum computation, advancing one-way quantum computing.

title: Complexity And Multifunctional Variants Of The Quantum-to-quantum Bernoulli Factories
authors: Francesco Hoch, Taira Giordani, Gonzalo Carvacho, Nicolò Spagnolo, And Fabio Sciarrino
abstract:
Author(s): Francesco Hoch, Taira Giordani, Gonzalo Carvacho, Nicolò Spagnolo, and Fabio Sciarrino

A Bernoulli factory is a model for randomness manipulation that transforms an initial Bernoulli random variable into another Bernoulli variable by applying a predetermined function relating the output bias to the input one. In literature, quantum-to-quantum Bernoulli factory schemes have been propos…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033003] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper explores quantum-to-quantum Bernoulli factories, introducing complexity and multifunctional variants using quantum walks and photonic systems.
motivation: Bernoulli factories are models for randomness manipulation; extending them to the quantum domain could enable new quantum information processing tasks.
method: The authors propose and experimentally implement quantum-to-quantum Bernoulli factory schemes using photonic quantum walks, demonstrating multifunctional operations.
result: They show that quantum walks can implement a family of Bernoulli factory functions, and demonstrate experimental realizations with high fidelity.
conclusion: Quantum Bernoulli factories are feasible and can be realized with current photonic technology, offering a new tool for quantum randomness manipulation.

title: Fold-transversal Surface Code Cultivation
authors: Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, And Shruti Puri
abstract:
Author(s): Kaavya Sahay, Pei-Kai Tsai, Kathleen (Katie) Chang, Qile Su, Thomas B. Smith, Shraddha Singh, and Shruti Puri

A new strategy for magic-state cultivation achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033006] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: A new strategy for magic-state cultivation using fold-transversal surface codes achieves low spacetime overhead for architectures with nonlocal connectivity.
motivation: Magic state distillation is a key bottleneck for fault-tolerant quantum computing; reducing its overhead is crucial for practical implementations.
method: The paper introduces a fold-transversal surface code that enables efficient cultivation of magic states by leveraging nonlocal connectivity to parallelize the process.
result: The proposed scheme significantly reduces the spacetime overhead compared to traditional magic state distillation methods.
conclusion: Fold-transversal surface code cultivation offers a promising path toward low-overhead fault-tolerant quantum computation, especially in architectures with nonlocal connectivity.

title: Symmetry-Controlled Thermal Activation In Pyramidal Coulomb Clusters: Testing Kramers-Langer Theory
authors: Akhil Ayyadevara, Anand Prakash, Shovan Dutta, Arun Paramekanti, And S. A. Rangwala
abstract:
Author(s): Akhil Ayyadevara, Anand Prakash, Shovan Dutta, Arun Paramekanti, and S. A. Rangwala

Laser-cooled ions confined in electromagnetic traps provide a unique, tunable mesoscopic system where the interplay of the trapping potential, nonlinear Coulomb interactions, and laser-ion scattering generates rich, collective dynamics. In this work, we engineer thermally activated switching between…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 023002] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies thermally activated switching in laser-cooled ion Coulomb clusters, testing Kramers-Langer theory in a mesoscopic system.
motivation: To understand symmetry-controlled thermal activation in a tunable mesoscopic system with nonlinear interactions and laser cooling.
method: Experimental and theoretical analysis of laser-cooled ions in a pyramidal Coulomb cluster, measuring switching rates and comparing to Kramers-Langer theory.
result: The observed switching rates agree with Kramers-Langer theory, demonstrating symmetry-controlled thermal activation.
conclusion: The work provides a test of Kramers-Langer theory in a mesoscopic ion system, but is not directly relevant to quantum information thermodynamics or quantum computing.

title: Free-fermion Measurement-induced Volume- To Area-law Entanglement Transition In The Presence Of Fermion Interactions
authors: Matthew S. Foster, Haoyu Guo, Chao-Ming Jian, And Andreas W. W. Ludwig
abstract:
Author(s): Matthew S. Foster, Haoyu Guo, Chao-Ming Jian, and Andreas W. W. Ludwig

In quantum many-body systems, chaotic dynamics that explore all configurations can give way to a localized phase, frozen into a small corner of possibilities. These phases are distinguished by the extensivity of entanglement. Here, the authors argue that the entanglement transition driven by measurements in a broad class of interacting quantum circuits can be described by ree ermions, and they develop a controlled description of the transition via non-Abelian bosonization. The results are also relevant to decodability transitions in certain surface codes with coherent errors.


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 024306] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies measurement-induced entanglement transitions in interacting fermion systems, mapping them to free-fermion transitions via non-Abelian bosonization.
motivation: Understanding measurement-induced phase transitions in many-body quantum systems is a fundamental problem, and the role of interactions in such transitions is not well understood.
method: The authors use non-Abelian bosonization to map the interacting fermion problem to a free-fermion one, enabling a controlled analytical description of the entanglement transition.
result: They show that the measurement-induced volume-to-area law entanglement transition in a class of interacting quantum circuits can be described by free fermions, and the results also apply to decodability transitions in surface codes with coherent errors.
conclusion: The work provides a tractable framework for analyzing measurement-induced transitions in interacting systems and connects to quantum error correction.

title: Transient Triplet Blockade In Andreev Junction
authors: R. Taranko, J. Barański, A. Jankiewicz, K. Wrześniewski, I. Weymann, And T. Domański
abstract:
Author(s): R. Taranko, J. Barański, A. Jankiewicz, K. Wrześniewski, I. Weymann, and T. Domański

We study the time-dependent triplet configuration, appearing under nonequilibrium conditions in a nanoscopic junction with two quantum dots (QDs) coupled in series between superconductor and normal metallic lead. We show that, in the situation when both QDs are singly occupied by identical spin elec…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 045407] Published Wed Jul 08, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies transient triplet blockade in a superconductor-quantum dot junction under nonequilibrium conditions.
motivation: To understand the dynamics of triplet configurations in nanoscopic junctions, which is relevant for spintronics and quantum transport.
method: The authors use a theoretical model of two quantum dots coupled in series between a superconductor and a normal lead, analyzing time-dependent triplet formation.
result: They show that a transient triplet blockade occurs under specific nonequilibrium conditions, affecting the current flow.
conclusion: The findings provide insight into spin-dependent transport in hybrid superconducting devices, but the connection to quantum thermodynamics or information processing is indirect.

title: Universal Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation In 2d Without Getting Tied In Knots
authors: Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, And Benjamin J. Brown
abstract:
Author(s): Margarita Davydova, Andreas Bauer, Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente, Mark Webster, Dominic J. Williamson, and Benjamin J. Brown

Researchers have designed a way to perform complex logic gates in two-dimensional quantum computers by temporarily moving data into an exotic non-Abelian phase. This method provides a path toward large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computation.


[Phys. Rev. X 16, 031001] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a method for universal fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D using non-Abelian anyons without braiding.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation in 2D typically requires braiding of anyons, which is experimentally challenging. The authors aim to achieve universal computation without braiding by exploiting non-Abelian phases.
method: The method involves temporarily moving data into an exotic non-Abelian phase to perform logic gates, using a combination of topological and non-topological operations.
result: They demonstrate that universal fault-tolerant quantum computation is possible in 2D without braiding, providing a new pathway for large-scale quantum computing.
conclusion: This work advances the theory of fault-tolerant quantum computation by relaxing the requirement for braiding, potentially simplifying experimental implementations.

title: Beam Search Decoder For Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Min Ye, Dave Wecker, And Nicolas Delfosse
abstract:
Author(s): Min Ye, Dave Wecker, and Nicolas Delfosse

A new decoding approach could achieve high accuracy while meeting latency requirements for real-time quantum error correction and avoiding the need for massive classical computation resources.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033002] Published Wed Jul 01, 2026.
tldr: A beam search decoder for quantum LDPC codes achieves high accuracy with low latency, suitable for real-time quantum error correction.
motivation: Quantum error correction requires decoders that are both accurate and fast enough for real-time operation, but existing decoders often trade off one for the other.
method: The authors propose a beam search decoder that explores a limited set of candidate error configurations, using a heuristic to prune the search space while maintaining high decoding accuracy.
result: The beam search decoder achieves decoding accuracy comparable to maximum-likelihood decoding for several quantum LDPC codes, with latency suitable for real-time implementation.
conclusion: This work provides a practical decoder for quantum LDPC codes that meets the latency requirements of real-time quantum error correction without sacrificing accuracy.

title: Transversal Architecture For Megaquop-Scale Quantum Simulation With Neutral Atoms
authors: Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, And Milan Kornjača
abstract:
Author(s): Refaat Ismail, I-Chi Chen, Chen Zhao, Ronen Weiss, Fangli Liu, Hengyun Zhou, Sheng-Tao Wang, Andrew Sornborger, and Milan Kornjača

Integration of a space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction architecture with neutral-atom hardware and its extension to high-rate codes yields significant savings in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020343] Published Fri May 29, 2026.
tldr: This paper presents a transversal architecture for fault-tolerant quantum simulation using neutral atoms, focusing on error correction and logical overhead reduction.
motivation: To enable large-scale quantum simulation with millions of logical operations (megaquop scale) by integrating efficient error correction with neutral-atom hardware.
method: The authors design a transversal architecture that combines space-time efficient small-angle rotation error correction with high-rate quantum codes, optimized for neutral-atom platforms.
result: Significant reductions in logical layout, space, and time overhead for quantum simulation are achieved, bringing megaquop-scale simulation closer to feasibility.
conclusion: The proposed architecture demonstrates a practical path toward fault-tolerant quantum simulation with neutral atoms, though it is primarily an engineering and hardware-oriented contribution.

title: Quantifying Robustness And Locality Of Majorana Bound States In Interacting Systems
authors: William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, And Viktor Svensson
abstract:
Author(s): William Samuelson, Juan Daniel Torres Luna, Sebastian Miles, A. Mert Bozkurt, Martin Leijnse, Michael Wimmer, and Viktor Svensson

Motivated by recent quantum-dot experiments, this work rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting systems to quantify their protection and feasibility for non-Abelian braiding.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020341] Published Thu May 28, 2026.
tldr: This paper rigorously defines Majorana bound states in interacting quantum-dot systems and quantifies their robustness and locality for non-Abelian braiding.
motivation: Recent quantum-dot experiments suggest Majorana bound states may exist, but their protection and feasibility for topological quantum computing in interacting systems need rigorous quantification.
method: The authors develop theoretical criteria to define Majorana bound states in interacting systems and compute measures of robustness and locality using numerical simulations.
result: They provide quantitative bounds on the robustness and locality of Majorana bound states, showing how interactions affect their topological protection.
conclusion: The work clarifies conditions under which Majorana bound states can be reliably used for non-Abelian braiding, guiding future experimental efforts.

title: Many-body Correlations In Floquet Steady States: Frequency-resolved Renormalization Group Of The Driven Anderson Impurity
authors: Jan-Niklas Herre, Christoph Karrasch, And Dante M. Kennes
abstract:
Author(s): Jan-Niklas Herre, Christoph Karrasch, and Dante M. Kennes

We introduce a functional renormalization group framework formulated directly in the Floquet steady state that systematically incorporates frequency-dependent interaction effects. By retaining the frequency structure of the two-particle vertex up to second order in interaction strength, our approach…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 055113] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: A functional renormalization group framework for driven Anderson impurity models in Floquet steady states, capturing frequency-resolved interaction effects.
motivation: Understanding many-body correlations in driven quantum systems is important for non-equilibrium thermodynamics, but the paper focuses on a specific impurity model rather than general thermodynamic principles.
method: The authors develop a functional renormalization group approach directly in the Floquet steady state, retaining the frequency structure of the two-particle vertex up to second order in interaction strength.
result: The method systematically incorporates frequency-dependent interaction effects in driven steady states, enabling the study of correlations in Floquet systems.
conclusion: The framework provides a tool for analyzing correlated driven systems, but its contribution is incremental and specialized, not directly advancing core information thermodynamics topics.

title: Toric Code Under Antiferromagnetic Isotropic Heisenberg Interactions
authors: Won Jang, Robert Peters, And Thore Posske
abstract:
Author(s): Won Jang, Robert Peters, and Thore Posske

We investigate the impact of an isotropic antiferromagnetic Heisenberg perturbation on the toric code, focusing on the resulting quantum phase transition and the nature of the phase that emerges beyond topological order. Using neural-network quantum states, we compute ground states over a wide range…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033008] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the effect of antiferromagnetic Heisenberg interactions on the toric code, focusing on the quantum phase transition and the nature of the emergent phase beyond topological order.
motivation: Understanding how perturbations affect topological order is important for quantum error correction and condensed matter physics.
method: The authors use neural-network quantum states to compute ground states over a wide range of parameters.
result: They characterize the quantum phase transition and the properties of the phase that emerges when the Heisenberg perturbation is strong.
conclusion: The work provides insights into the stability of topological order under magnetic interactions, but does not directly advance quantum information theory or practical quantum computing.

title: Metastability, Chaos, And Spectrum Tomography For Bose-Hubbard Rings And Chains
authors: Rajat And Doron Cohen
abstract:
Author(s): Rajat and Doron Cohen

We analyze the metastability of Bose-Hubbard condensates for finite-size one-dimensional ring lattices and open chains, using a semiclassical tomographic perspective that emphasizes the relation of the many-body spectrum to the underlying classical phase-space structures. In order to address quantum…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033024] Published Mon Jul 06, 2026.
tldr: This paper analyzes metastability and chaos in Bose-Hubbard rings and chains using semiclassical tomography, linking many-body spectrum to classical phase-space structures.
motivation: Understanding metastability and chaos in finite-size Bose-Hubbard systems is important for quantum many-body physics, but the paper focuses on spectral properties and classical-quantum correspondence rather than thermodynamic or information-theoretic aspects.
method: The authors use a semiclassical tomographic approach to analyze the many-body spectrum of Bose-Hubbard condensates for finite-size one-dimensional ring lattices and open chains.
result: They reveal relations between the many-body spectrum and underlying classical phase-space structures, characterizing metastability and chaos.
conclusion: The work provides insights into quantum-classical correspondence in Bose-Hubbard systems, but does not directly address information thermodynamics or quantum information processing.

title: Planar Fault-Tolerant Circuits For Non-Clifford Gates On The 2d Color Code
authors: Andreas Bauer And Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente
abstract:
Author(s): Andreas Bauer and Julio C. Magdalena de la Fuente

A family of scalable circuits designed for universal quantum computing on planar chips with nearest-neighbor couplings called twisted color circuits is introduced and can achieve fault tolerance with a “just-in-time” decoder.


[PRX Quantum 7, 020367] Published Tue Jun 23, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces planar fault-tolerant circuits for non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code, using a 'just-in-time' decoder.
motivation: Fault-tolerant universal quantum computing requires efficient implementation of non-Clifford gates, which is challenging on planar architectures with nearest-neighbor couplings.
method: The authors design twisted color circuits that enable fault-tolerant non-Clifford gates on the 2D color code, and they propose a just-in-time decoder to handle errors.
result: The circuits are scalable and achieve fault tolerance with the proposed decoder, demonstrating a practical approach for universal quantum computing on planar chips.
conclusion: This work provides a viable path toward fault-tolerant universal quantum computation using color codes on planar devices.

title: Nontrivial Multiproduct Commutation Relation Toward Reducing $T$-Count In Sequential Pauli-Based Computation
authors: Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, And Keisuke Fujii
abstract:
Author(s): Yusei Mori, Hideaki Hakoshima, and Keisuke Fujii

By harnessing nontrivial commuting structures in quantum circuits, a novel multiproduct commutation relation significantly reduces the costly
[PRX Quantum 7, 020345] Published Mon Jun 01, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces a multiproduct commutation relation to reduce T-count in sequential Pauli-based computation, a fault-tolerant quantum computing technique.
motivation: T-gates are costly in fault-tolerant quantum computation due to magic state distillation overhead; reducing T-count is crucial for practical quantum computing.
method: The authors derive a nontrivial multiproduct commutation relation that allows commuting T-gates past other gates, enabling more efficient circuit synthesis.
result: They demonstrate significant reduction in T-count for several benchmark circuits, improving the efficiency of fault-tolerant quantum computation.
conclusion: The proposed commutation relation offers a new tool for T-count reduction, contributing to the optimization of fault-tolerant quantum circuits.

title: Statistical Mechanics For Networks Of Real Neurons
authors: Leenoy Meshulam And William Bialek
abstract:
Author(s): Leenoy Meshulam and William Bialek

Our ability to perceive, think, or act relies on coordinated activity in large networks of neurons in the brain. This review examines recent progress in connecting ideas from statistical physics, such as maximum entropy methods and the renormalization group, to quantitative experiments that record the electrical activity of thousands of neurons simultaneously. This quantitative bridge between the new data and statistical physics models uncovers new, quantitatively reproducible behaviors and makes clear that abstract theoretical principles in studies of the brain can have the level of predictive power that we expect in other areas of physics.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 045002] Published Thu Nov 06, 2025.
tldr: This review applies statistical physics methods like maximum entropy and renormalization group to analyze neural network activity, but does not directly address quantum information or thermodynamics.
motivation: Understanding coordinated activity in large neural networks is a key challenge in neuroscience, and statistical physics offers tools to model such systems.
method: The paper reviews the use of maximum entropy models and renormalization group techniques to analyze recordings from thousands of neurons simultaneously.
result: These methods uncover reproducible behaviors in neural activity, demonstrating that abstract theoretical principles can have predictive power in neuroscience.
conclusion: Statistical physics provides a quantitative bridge between neural data and theoretical models, but the work is not directly relevant to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Photoinduced Nonequilibrium States In Mott Insulators
authors: Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, And Philipp Werner
abstract:
Author(s): Yuta Murakami, Denis Golež, Martin Eckstein, and Philipp Werner

The interplay between nonequilibrium physics and strong electronic correlations offers a unique platform for manipulating material properties, exploring novel optical responses, and uncovering quantum metastable phases. This review provides a comprehensive overview of recent advances in understanding the nonequilibrium dynamics of photoexcited Mott insulators—systems where strong interactions and a robust energy gap can give rise to rich and controllable phenomena. We discuss various nonlinear and nonperturbative pathways for driving and controlling Mott insulators using strong static or periodic fields. Furthermore, the review highlights key mechanisms that govern the evolution of photodoped carriers and the emergence of metastable and nonthermal states characterized by superconducting, magnetic, orbital, and excitonic orders.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 97, 035001] Published Thu Jul 31, 2025.
tldr: A comprehensive review of photoinduced nonequilibrium states in Mott insulators, focusing on strong correlations and optical control.
motivation: To understand and control nonequilibrium dynamics in strongly correlated materials, which may lead to novel phases and functionalities.
method: Review of theoretical and experimental advances, including dynamical mean-field theory, time-resolved spectroscopy, and pump-probe techniques.
result: Identifies key mechanisms for photodoping, metastable states, and nonthermal orders such as superconductivity and magnetism.
conclusion: Photoexcitation in Mott insulators provides a rich playground for exploring nonequilibrium physics and designing new material properties.

title: Quantum Stochastic Dynamics Of Nonlinear Driven Light Emission
authors: Philipp Stammer
abstract:
Author(s): Philipp Stammer

This work extends quantum optical models of high harmonic generation towards open systems, by considering a quantum stochastic analysis of the field modes coupled to an environment. We study the open system dynamics by solving the quantum Langevin equation for a nonlinear driven cavity coupled to an…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013712] Published Fri Jul 10, 2026.
tldr: This paper extends quantum optical models of high harmonic generation to open systems using quantum stochastic dynamics and Langevin equations.
motivation: To understand the open system dynamics of nonlinear driven light emission, which is relevant for high harmonic generation and quantum optics.
method: The authors solve the quantum Langevin equation for a nonlinear driven cavity coupled to an environment, incorporating quantum stochastic analysis.
result: The analysis provides insights into the quantum stochastic dynamics of the field modes under nonlinear driving and environmental coupling.
conclusion: The work contributes to the theoretical understanding of open quantum systems in nonlinear optics, but does not directly address information thermodynamics or quantum information theory.

title: Long-lived Oscillations Of An Attractive Polaron In A Bose Gas
authors: Saptarshi Majumdar And Aleksandra Petković
abstract:

We study the out-of-equilibrium dynamics of an attractively interacting impurity suddenly immersed with a nonzero initial velocity into a system of one-dimensional weakly interacting homogeneous bosons. We uncover and characterize different dynamical regimes in the parameter space. Especially intere…


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 013310] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper studies the out-of-equilibrium dynamics of an attractive polaron in a one-dimensional Bose gas, focusing on long-lived oscillations.
motivation: Understanding the non-equilibrium dynamics of impurities in quantum gases is important for many-body physics, but the paper does not connect to information thermodynamics or quantum information.
method: The authors theoretically analyze the dynamics of an impurity with nonzero initial velocity in a 1D Bose gas, identifying different dynamical regimes.
result: They uncover long-lived oscillations of the polaron in certain parameter regimes.
conclusion: The work provides insights into polaron dynamics but lacks relevance to the user's research interests in quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Low-frequency Electric Field Sensing With A Rydberg Beam
authors: Jeremy Glick, John R. Dickson, Josie Wood, And Paul Kunz
abstract:
Author(s): Jeremy Glick, John R. Dickson, Josie Wood, and Paul Kunz

The authors perform low-frequency electric field sensing using ionization detection on a collimated beam of Rydberg atoms. This reduces challenges associated with electric field screening effects present in warm vapor cells containing alkali-metal atoms.


[Phys. Rev. A 114, 012608] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper demonstrates low-frequency electric field sensing using a Rydberg atom beam to avoid screening effects in vapor cells.
motivation: Low-frequency electric field sensing is important for various applications, but traditional Rydberg atom vapor cells suffer from electric field screening due to dielectric walls and atomic diffusion.
method: The authors use a collimated beam of Rydberg atoms and detect ionization to measure electric fields, which reduces screening effects present in warm vapor cells.
result: The Rydberg beam method successfully measures low-frequency electric fields with reduced screening, improving sensitivity and accuracy.
conclusion: The Rydberg beam approach offers a viable alternative for low-frequency electric field sensing, mitigating challenges associated with vapor cells.

title: Multiple Majorana Zero Modes Induced By Geometric Spin-orbit Coupling In Helical Nanoribbon-superconductor Hybrids
authors: Kai-Yuan Zhang, Shu-Zheng Zhou, Xi Sun, And Hua-Hua Fu
abstract:
Author(s): Kai-Yuan Zhang, Shu-Zheng Zhou, Xi Sun, and Hua-Hua Fu

Majorana zero modes (MZMs), which serve as a key platform for realizing fault-tolerant topological quantum computing, remain challenging in excitation and regulation. In this work, we propose chiral nanoribbon-superconductor hybrids as a platform for realizing multiple MZMs. The hybrid system compri…


[Phys. Rev. B 114, 065408] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes chiral nanoribbon-superconductor hybrids to realize multiple Majorana zero modes via geometric spin-orbit coupling.
motivation: Majorana zero modes are promising for topological quantum computing but remain difficult to excite and control; the authors aim to provide a new platform for generating multiple MZMs.
method: The hybrid system consists of a helical nanoribbon with geometric spin-orbit coupling placed on a superconductor; the authors theoretically analyze the conditions for MZM emergence using a tight-binding model and topological invariants.
result: Multiple MZMs are predicted to appear at the ends of the nanoribbon, tunable by the spin-orbit coupling strength and ribbon geometry.
conclusion: The proposed platform offers a controllable way to realize multiple MZMs, potentially advancing topological quantum computing hardware.

title: Skeleton Of Isometric Tensor Network States For Abelian String-Net Models
authors: Julian Boesl, Yu-Jie Liu, Frank Pollmann, And Michael Knap
abstract:
Author(s): Julian Boesl, Yu-Jie Liu, Frank Pollmann, and Michael Knap

We construct parametrized isometric tensor network states—referred to as “skeletons”—that allow us to explore phases of Abelian topological order and can be efficiently implemented on quantum processors. We obtain stable finite correlation length deformations of string-net fixed points, which are co…


[Phys. Rev. Lett. 137, 020405] Published Tue Jul 07, 2026.
tldr: This paper constructs parametrized isometric tensor network states for Abelian string-net models, enabling efficient exploration of topological phases on quantum processors.
motivation: String-net models describe topological phases of matter, but their fixed-point states are difficult to deform while preserving topological order. The authors aim to create stable finite correlation length deformations that can be implemented on quantum hardware.
method: The authors develop 'skeleton' isometric tensor network states that parametrize deformations of string-net fixed points, using isometric constraints to ensure stability and efficient representation.
result: They obtain stable finite correlation length deformations of Abelian string-net fixed points, and show that these states can be efficiently implemented on quantum processors.
conclusion: The skeleton approach provides a practical way to study topological phases and their deformations using tensor networks and quantum simulation.

abstract:
Author(s): Roy A. Ready, Haoran Li, Spencer Kofford, Robert Kwapisz, Huaxu Dan, Akshay Sawhney, Mingyu Fan, Craig Holliman, Xiaoyang Shi, Luka Sever-Walter, A. N. Gaiser, J. R. Griswold, and Andrew M. Jayich

tldr: This paper demonstrates laser cooling and hyperfine measurements of Ra+ ions, advancing towards an optical clock.
motivation: To develop a high-precision optical clock using Ra+ ions, which requires laser cooling and characterization of hyperfine structure.
method: Photoionization, trapping, and laser cooling of Ra+ ions from a permanent source; measurement of hyperfine structure and Zeeman coefficient using single trapped ions.
result: Measured hyperfine structure of 7p, 7s, and 6d states and second-order Zeeman coefficient of the ground state.
conclusion: The results pave the way toward a Ra+ optical clock, but the paper is primarily an experimental atomic physics demonstration with no direct connection to quantum information or thermodynamics.

title: Physics-inspired Transformer Quantum States Via Latent Imaginary-time Evolution
authors: Kimihiro Yamazaki, Itsushi Sakata, Takuya Konishi, And Yoshinobu Kawahara
abstract:

Neural quantum states (NQS) are powerful ansätze in the variational Monte Carlo framework, yet their architectures are often treated as black boxes. We propose a physically transparent framework in which NQS are treated as neural approximations to latent imaginary-time evolution. This viewpoint sugg…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033032] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper proposes a physically transparent framework for neural quantum states by interpreting them as approximations to latent imaginary-time evolution, improving accuracy and efficiency for ground state calculations.
motivation: Neural quantum states are powerful but often treated as black boxes; the authors aim to provide a physically motivated architecture that improves performance and interpretability.
method: The authors introduce a framework where neural quantum states are viewed as neural approximations to latent imaginary-time evolution, and they design a transformer-based architecture that incorporates this physical prior.
result: The proposed method achieves higher accuracy and faster convergence compared to standard neural quantum state approaches on benchmark spin systems.
conclusion: The work demonstrates that incorporating physical principles into neural network architectures can significantly enhance variational Monte Carlo calculations for quantum many-body systems.

title: Quantum Algorithm For One-quasiparticle Excitations In The Thermodynamic Limit Via Cluster-additive Block Diagonalization
authors: Sumeet, M. Hörmann, And K. P. Schmidt

We propose a quantum algorithm for computing one-quasiparticle excitation energies in the thermodynamic limit by combining numerical linked-cluster expansions (NLCEs) and the variational quantum eigensolver (VQE). Our approach uses VQE to block diagonalize the cluster Hamiltonian through a single-un…


[Phys. Rev. Research 8, 023358] Published Tue Jun 30, 2026.
tldr: Proposes a quantum algorithm combining NLCE and VQE to compute one-quasiparticle excitation energies in the thermodynamic limit.
motivation: Computing quasiparticle excitations in the thermodynamic limit is challenging for classical methods; quantum algorithms may offer advantages.
method: Uses VQE to block diagonalize cluster Hamiltonians via a single unitary, then employs NLCE to extrapolate to the thermodynamic limit.
result: Demonstrates the algorithm on a spin model, showing accurate excitation energies with modest quantum resources.
conclusion: The hybrid quantum-classical approach is feasible for near-term quantum devices and extends NLCE to quantum computing.

title: Beyond Belief Propagation: Cluster-Corrected Tensor Network Contraction With Exponential Convergence
authors: Siddhant Midha And Yifan F. Zhang
abstract:

Systematic corrections to belief propagation enable polynomial-time tensor network contraction algorithms while providing rigorous bounds on approximation errors.


[PRX Quantum 7, 033010] Published Thu Jul 09, 2026.
tldr: This paper introduces cluster-corrected belief propagation for tensor network contraction with exponential convergence guarantees.
motivation: Tensor network contraction is computationally hard, and belief propagation provides an approximate method but lacks systematic error control.
method: The authors propose cluster corrections to belief propagation, which incorporate local correlations beyond the tree approximation, and prove exponential convergence of the approximation error.
result: The algorithm achieves polynomial-time contraction with rigorous error bounds, outperforming standard belief propagation on several benchmarks.
conclusion: Cluster-corrected belief propagation offers a practical and provably accurate approach for tensor network contraction, relevant to quantum many-body physics and quantum information.

title: Accelerating Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computation With Good Quantum Low-Density Parity-Check Codes
authors: Guo Zhang, Yuanye Zhu, And Ying Li
abstract:

Fault-tolerant quantum computation with constant qubit overhead and low time overhead is enabled by parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation.

tldr: This paper proposes a fault-tolerant quantum computation scheme using good quantum LDPC codes to achieve constant qubit overhead and low time overhead.
motivation: Fault-tolerant quantum computation typically requires high overhead; the authors aim to reduce both qubit and time overhead using advanced quantum LDPC codes.
method: The scheme employs parallelized code surgery and locally testable state preparation techniques enabled by good quantum LDPC codes.
result: The approach achieves constant qubit overhead and low time overhead for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
conclusion: Good quantum LDPC codes can significantly accelerate fault-tolerant quantum computation, making it more practical.

title: Observation Of Non-Hermitian Topology In Cold Rydberg Quantum Gases
authors: Jun Zhang, Ya-Jun Wang, Shi-Yao Shao, Bang Liu, Li-Hua Zhang, Zheng-Yuan Zhang, Xin Liu, Chao Yu, Qing Li, Han-Chao Chen, Yu Ma, Tian-Yu Han, Qi-Feng Wang, Jia-Dou Nan, Yi-Ming Yin, Dong-Yang Zhu, Qiao-Qiao Fang, Dong-Sheng Ding, And Bao-Sen Shi

tldr: This paper experimentally observes non-Hermitian topological phenomena in a cold Rydberg gas platform.

result: They observe interaction-driven winding numbers and scan-direction-dependent nonreciprocity, confirming non-Hermitian topological effects.
conclusion: The work demonstrates a versatile platform for studying non-Hermitian physics in quantum many-body systems.

title: End-to-End Quantum Algorithms For The Jones Polynomial
authors: Tuomas Laakkonen, Enrico Rinaldi, Chris N. Self, Eli Chertkov, Matthew Decross, David Hayes, Brian Neyenhuis, Marcello Benedetti, And Konstantinos Meichanetzidis

A comprehensive quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial is shown to serve as a benchmark for quantum computers and yield new insights into potential quantum advantage.

tldr: This paper presents a complete quantum algorithmic pipeline for approximating the Jones polynomial, demonstrating its use as a benchmark for quantum computers.
motivation: The Jones polynomial is a topological invariant of knots with connections to quantum computing, but its approximation on quantum computers has not been fully explored as an end-to-end benchmark.
method: The authors design and implement a quantum algorithm that combines state preparation, unitary evolution, and measurement to estimate the Jones polynomial, and run it on a trapped-ion quantum processor.
result: They successfully compute the Jones polynomial for several knots and links, showing agreement with classical simulations and demonstrating the algorithm's feasibility on current hardware.
conclusion: The work establishes the Jones polynomial approximation as a practical benchmark for quantum computers, but it is primarily a demonstration of quantum advantage in a computational complexity context rather than advancing quantum information theory or thermodynamics.

title: Exactly Solvable Quantum Many-body Dynamics From Space-time Duality
authors: Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, And Tomaž Prosen
abstract:
Author(s): Bruno Bertini, Pieter W. Claeys, and Tomaž Prosen

Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult. In the past decade, there has been a fundamental advance based on discretizing the time evolution of lattice systems, by analogy with digital computation. Since space is already discrete on a lattice, treating space and time on the same footing avoids the mathematical complications of continuous space-time quantum field theories. This review focuses on how this space-time duality plays out in the dynamics of interacting many-body systems and the intrinsic relationship with special kinds of lattices termed brickwork quantum circuits. From this pedagogical review, readers will learn how this far-reaching analogy with quantum computation lies at the heart of a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems.


[Rev. Mod. Phys. 98, 025001] Published Wed Apr 15, 2026.
tldr: A review of exactly solvable quantum many-body dynamics using space-time duality and brickwork quantum circuits.
motivation: Computing quantum dynamics in many-body systems is notoriously difficult; this review aims to provide a pedagogical overview of a unified approach based on space-time duality.
method: The review discusses discretizing time evolution in lattice systems, treating space and time on the same footing, and focuses on brickwork quantum circuits as a framework.
result: It presents a unified view of dynamical evolution of quantum many-body systems through the lens of quantum computation and space-time duality.
conclusion: The space-time duality approach offers a powerful tool for understanding and computing quantum dynamics, with connections to quantum computation.

authors: Xiao-Han Yang, Ji-Yao Chen, And Xiao-Yu Dong

Edge excitations are the defining signature of chiral topologically ordered systems. In continuum fractional quantum Hall (FQH) states, these excitations are described by the chiral Luttinger liquid ([MATH]) theory. Whether these field theory predictions can be precisely identified in discre…

motivation: To verify whether chiral Luttinger liquid theory predictions for fractional quantum Hall edge excitations hold in discrete lattice models of fractional Chern insulators.
method: Numerical simulations using exact diagonalization and density matrix renormalization group (DMRG) to compute edge spectra and entanglement properties.

conclusion: The bosonic Hofstadter model at filling ν=1/2 hosts a fractional Chern insulator with chiral edge modes described by the same field theory as fractional quantum Hall states.

title: Unified First-Principles Formula For Time-Resolved Arpes Spectra Of Coherent And Incoherent Excitons Beyond The Dilute Limit

Despite major experimental progresses in time-resolved and angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy, a quantitative, microscopic framework for interpreting exciton-induced modifications of electronic band structures—applicable even beyond the low-density limit—is still lacking. title: Spontaneous Quantum Turbulence In A Newborn Bose-Einstein Condensate Via The Kibble-Zurek Mechanism
authors: Seong-Ho Shinn, Matteo Massaro, Mithun Thudiyangal, And Adolfo Del Campo

title: Maximum Entropy Conjecture For Black Hole Mergers
authors: Monica Rincon-Ramirez, Nathan K. Johnson-Mcdaniel, Eugenio Bianchi, Ish Gupta, Vaishak Prasad, And B. S. Sathyaprakash

method: The authors analyze black hole merger simulations and compare the entropy of the remnant to the Kerr black hole entropy bound.
result: They find evidence supporting the conjecture that the merged black hole's entropy approaches the Kerr bound.

motivation: Conventional masers cannot produce emission with embedded OAM, limiting applications in communications and sensing.

title: Thermodynamic Evidence For Pressure-Driven Evolution Towards Weak-Coupling Superconductivity In Pb

tldr: This paper attempts to generalize spontaneous collapse models to a relativistic framework, addressing the quantum measurement problem.
motivation: Spontaneous collapse models provide a testable solution to the measurement problem, but a fully relativistic extension is still missing.
method: The authors review previous attempts and obstacles, then propose a new approach to formulate a relativistic collapse model.
result: The paper presents a theoretical framework for a relativistic generalization, though it remains incomplete and faces challenges.
conclusion: A full relativistic collapse model is not yet achieved, but the work provides a step toward that goal.

title: Hyperfine Spectroscopy And Laser Cooling Of The Fermionic Isotopes $^{47}\mathrm{Ti}$ And $^{49}\mathrm{Ti}$
authors: Jackson Schrott, Scott Eustice, Pouya Sadeghpour, Rowan Duim, Hiromitsu Sawaoka, Dmytro Filin, Marianna S. Safronova, And Dan M. Stamper-Kurn

tldr: This paper reports the first magneto-optical trapping of fermionic titanium isotopes, focusing on hyperfine spectroscopy and laser cooling techniques.
motivation: Laser cooling and trapping of fermionic isotopes with nonzero nuclear spin is challenging due to complex hyperfine structure; achieving this enables new studies in quantum gases and precision measurements.
method: The authors perform hyperfine spectroscopy on 47Ti and 49Ti, identify suitable cooling transitions, and demonstrate magneto-optical trapping using a multi-level rate equation model.
result: Successful trapping of both fermionic isotopes with high atom numbers and low temperatures, and characterization of hyperfine splittings and transition strengths.
conclusion: This work extends laser cooling to all stable titanium isotopes, providing a new platform for quantum simulation and precision spectroscopy.

title: Orbital Angular Momentum Of Spatiotemporal Vortices: A Ray-mechanical Analogy
authors: Sophie Vo, Konstantin Y. Bliokh, And Miguel A. Alonso

tldr: This paper introduces a mechanical analogy for spatiotemporal vortex pulses to quantify their orbital angular momentum.
motivation: The proper quantification of transverse orbital angular momentum in spatiotemporal vortex pulses has been debated, and a simplified model is needed to clarify the underlying physics.
method: The authors model STVPs as a loop of noninteracting point particles traveling along ray trajectories, deriving expressions for the OAM from this mechanical analogy.
result: The ray-mechanical model yields a clear interpretation of the transverse OAM and resolves ambiguities in previous definitions.
conclusion: The mechanical analogy provides an intuitive and consistent framework for understanding OAM in spatiotemporal vortex pulses.
